Adaptive Deep Reinforcement Learning-Augmented Hybrid SMC-ANFIS Controller for Dynamic Voltage Restorer: Enhanced Power Quality Mitigation in Active Distribution Networks with Renewable Energy Integration
abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy resources and power electronic converters has intensified power quality disturbances in active distribution networks, necessitating intelligent Dynamic Voltage Restorers (DVRs) capable of rapid and adaptive voltage compensation. This paper proposes an Adaptive Deep Reinforcement Learning-assisted Hybrid Sliding Mode Controller integrated with an Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ADRL–HSMC–ANFIS) for DVR-based power quality enhancement. The proposed framework combines synchronous reference frame theory for voltage extraction, an ANFIS-based adaptive reference voltage generator, and a chattering-suppressed hybrid sliding mode controller whose control gains are continuously optimized using a Twin-Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) agent. In addition, a novel Integral Square Error with Rate-weighting (ISER) objective function is formulated to simultaneously minimize voltage regulation error and transient oscillations, thereby improving both transient response and steady-state performance. The proposed controller is validated on a modified IEEE 33-bus active distribution network integrated with a 1 MW photovoltaic generation system and a 500 kWh battery energy storage system under balanced and unbalanced voltage sag, voltage swell, dynamic load variation, and renewable intermittency. Simulation results demonstrate a voltage restoration time of 3.2 ms, load voltage regulation of 99.95 ± 0.05%, and a minimum voltage total harmonic distortion (THD) of 0.41%, while providing superior DC-link voltage regulation, reduced chattering, and enhanced robustness compared with conventional PI, PSO-PI, SMC, PSO-SMC, and DQN-SMC controllers. These results demonstrate that the proposed ADRL–HSMC–ANFIS framework provides an effective, adaptive, and computationally efficient control strategy for resilient power quality enhancement in renewable-integrated active distribution networks.

title: AI-assisted high-throughput screening of MOFs for formaldehyde capture.
abstract: Formaldehyde (FA) is a hazardous indoor volatile organic compound that poses risks to human health, demanding efficient adsorbent materials. Functionalized Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs) offer structural tunability; however, functionalization can alter the framework, increase heterogeneity, cause pore blockage, and increase cost. Identification of pristine MOFs for FA adsorption is crucial for understanding adsorption mechanisms, framework topology, chemical composition, and unfunctionalized structures.

title: Polysaccharide-dominant bigels for enhanced topical drug delivery: construction, mechanical properties, and release control
abstract: Bigels represent a class of biphasic cross-linked materials that offer superior control over the transdermal delivery of both hydrophilic and lipophilic drugs compared to single-phase counterparts, offering significant promise for biomedical applications. Bigels address a critical limitation of conventional carriers by enabling the simultaneous solubilization of both water-soluble and insoluble compounds.

title: From a High-T$\rm_C$ Spin-Gapless Semiconductor to a Spin-Glass: The Role of Disorder in NiMnCrAl
abstract: We combine first-principles calculations with structural, magnetic, and transport measurements to investigate the influence of chemical disorder on the quaternary Heusler alloy NiMnCrAl. For the ordered Y-type structure, density-functional-theory calculations predict a ferrimagnetic spin-gapless-semiconducting state with a total magnetic moment of $1.99\,μ_{\mathrm{B}}/\mathrm{f.u.}$ and a mean-field ordering temperature of approximately $1300~\mathrm{K}$. Polycrystalline NiMnCrAl forms in a single average cubic phase; however, combined x-ray diffraction, neutron diffraction, and extended x-ray absorption fine-structure measurements reveal substantial antisite disorder, characterized by predominantly B2-like disorder with additional cross-sublattice mixing. No long-range ferrimagnetic transition is observed up to $700~\mathrm{K}$. Instead, the compound exhibits a broad magnetic anomaly near $37~\mathrm{K}$, frequency-dependent ac susceptibility, slow stretched-exponential relaxation, and field-cooled and zero-field-cooled memory effects, establishing a glassy magnetic state. The electrical resistivity is metallic and the Seebeck coefficient is negative, consistent with the loss of the ideal spin-gapless electronic structure. Exchange-interaction calculations show that antisite disorder introduces short Mn--Mn separations and competing antiferromagnetic Mn--Mn and Mn--Cr interactions, providing a microscopic basis for magnetic frustration. These results demonstrate the strong sensitivity to the predicted spin-gapless and ferrimagnetic states of NiMnCrAl to chemical disorder.

title: Quantum-classical dynamical density functional theory for solvation dynamics
abstract: We provide a unified modeling framework for thermalization and non-equilibrium spectroscopy in overdamped polar environments. This framework extends dynamical density functional theory to describe the coupled quantum-classical evolution of a molecular electronic subsystem and an overdamped polar solvent represented by a reaction-field coordinate. The nonadiabatic dynamics is formulated in terms of an operator-valued distribution obeying a quantum-classical Ehrenfest--Smoluchowski equation which exhibits nonlinear classical diffusion and non-increasing free energy, thereby retaining detailed balance. In contrast, a quantum-classical Liouville--Smoluchowski model with quantum-classical linear diffusion develops unstable long-time behavior and fails to reach a stationary thermal state. The method is applied to a two-level model of a polar dye in three different solvents: chloroform, dichloromethane, and dimethyl sulfoxide, each differing in polarity and dielectric relaxation time. Absorption and time-resolved emission spectra are obtained from dipole-dipole correlation functions, capturing the solvent-induced spectral broadening, the dynamic Stokes shift, and the time evolution of the emission bandwidth. The calculated solvent spectral response agrees well with the experimental relaxation trends of the three solvents.

title: Canonical spin glass behavior and memory effects in van der Waals magnet (Fe0.55Ni0.45)3GaTe2
abstract: We demonstrate the canonical spin-glass behavior and non-equilibrium dynamics in a single-crystalline Ni-doped van der Waals magnet (Fe0.55Ni0.45)3GaTe2 with a freezing temperature $T_f \approx 45.5$ K from detailed ac susceptibility and dc magnetization measurements. The temperature-dependent dc magnetization exhibits strong magnetic irreversibility and the ac susceptibility shows that the peak at $T_f$ shifts towards higher temperatures with increase in ac frequency, indicating the presence of a spin glass state. The relative shift of the freezing temperature $δT_f$ per decade of frequency in ac susceptibility is estimated to be 0.0072. Dynamic scaling analysis of the frequency-dependent freezing temperature using the power law reveals the single spin flip relaxation time $τ_0=2\times10^{-13}$ s and critical exponent $zν=8.1$, while the Vogel-Fulcher law yields Vogel-Fulcher temperature $T_0=43$ K and activation energy $E_a/k_B=81$ K with $E_a/k_BT_0=1.88$. The obtained values of these characteristic parameters lie well within the range associated with a canonical spin glass. The detailed non-equilibrium dynamics study, involving the magnetic relaxation and memory effect, further confirms the glassy behavior. The memory effect in zero-field-cooled magnetization establishes that the glassy state arises from the cooperative spin-spin interaction and not from superparamagnetism. The asymmetric response of magnetic relaxation with respect to negative and positive temperature cycle favors the hierarchical model of memory effects over the droplet model.

title: Altermagnetism-induced magneto-optical effects
abstract: Altermagnets break time-reversal symmetry despite their zero net magnetization, enabling time-reversal-odd responses while retaining the advantages of antiferromagnets. However, magneto-optical (MO) effects are not universal among altermagnets because MO effects typically arise from magnetic dipole order (ferromagnetism), which is generally absent in altermagnets. In this work, we address this limitation by establishing octupolar MO effects, which arise from magnetic octupole order through spatial dispersion. Owing to this distinct origin, octupolar MO effects do not necessarily require spin-orbit coupling even in collinear magnets and can arise without an external magnetic field in antiferromagnets where conventional MO effects are symmetry-forbidden. Such antiferromagnets include $d$-wave altermagnets such as RuO$_2$ and KV$_2$Se$_2$O, certain $g$- and $i$-wave altermagnets, including CrSb, as well as noncoplanar antiferromagnets such as MnTe$_2$ and pyrochlore iridates with all-in-all-out magnetic order. From an experimental perspective, octupolar MO effects can reach detectable magnitudes and offer potential for magnetic-domain imaging, as supported by numerical calculations showing $μ$rad-scale Faraday rotation for a 100-nm-thick sample in the visible-light range and a sign reversal between opposite domains. Furthermore, octupolar MO effects are linked to an $f$-sum rule, enabling a quantitative estimate of the spin magnetic octupole moment from optical measurements. These results extend the scope of MO effects to a broad class of antiferromagnets, including altermagnets, and open a field-free optical route to exploring magnetic octupole order.

title: ForceBody: Force-Paired Parametric Body Motion with Torque Uncertainty
abstract: Forces and torques drive human motion, central to biomechanics, robotics, and physics-aware animation, yet they are often absent from learning-based motion pipelines for body reconstruction and generation. Some motion datasets provide force annotations, but the paired motion sequences are incompatible with the parametric body models used in modern learning pipelines. In addition, existing datasets typically obtain joint torques through inverse dynamics, which is inherently sensitive to the quality of the input kinematics; however, they do not quantify the reliability of these torque estimates. We close this gap with ForceBody, the first dataset to bring ground truth force supervision into a parametric body representation, shipped with per-sample torque uncertainty. ForceBody pairs the SKEL body model with ground reaction forces and inverse-dynamics joint torques across 10,386 motion trials (9.7M frames, 26.9 hours) from 140 subjects. Each torque label is paired with a per-frame, per-joint uncertainty annotation obtained by Monte Carlo sampling through the inverse dynamics pipeline. We benchmark six architectures (MLP, Conv1D, LSTM, GRU, Mamba2, Transformer) on ground reaction force and joint torque prediction from SKEL motion. As one example use of the released uncertainty, finetuning a Transformer with per-sample uncertainty weighting reduces the MAE of joint torque estimation by 5%. Code and data are at https://github.com/DominoAI-Lab/ForceBody-NeurIPS-ED-2026.

title: Universal scaling of brine migration in ice
abstract: Sea ice hosts mobile brine inclusions whose migration influences salt redistribution, microstructure and transport within the ice. Although their motion under temperature gradient is commonly described as a diffusion-limited process, experimental evidence has remained rare and insufficient because migration is slow and controlled inclusion seeding is challenging. Here we introduce an experimental method to trap and monitor hundreds of inclusions in ice under controlled temperature gradients. Using four solutes, three imposed gradients and two order of magnitude in initial concentration, we quantify migration dynamics over a broad range of conditions. We find that, except close to the ice front, inclusion migration is consistent with a regime limited by solute diffusion. After applying a universal scaling, both our data and previous measurements collapse onto a master curve, providing a general framework for describing solute transport in ice.

title: Interfacial electrostatics: From polar insulators to charged-layer metals
abstract: Polar discontinuities are typically described as arising from charged atomic planes, a spontaneous polarization, or a combination, in insulating films interfaced with vacuum, nonpolar insulators or metals. The resulting electrostatics are well established for systems such as LaAlO$_3$/SrTiO$_3$, BaTiO$_3$/SrRuO$_3$, and BiFeO$_3$/SrRuO$_3$. However, recent observations of "polar-discontinuity-like" behavior at interfaces in which the metal contains formally charged layers (e.g., rare-earth nickelates) challenge this picture. In this work, we summarize the theoretical framework used to define and quantify interface charge, layer polarization, and screening in the three reference systems above, and then discuss signatures attributed to the formal-charge polar discontinuity arising when SmNiO$_3$, a metal with formally charged (001) layers, is interfaced with ferroelectric BaTiO$_3$. We show how concepts developed for polar discontinuities between two insulators and for screening at metallic interfaces can rationalize the reported effects and identify where our understanding of these systems leaves open questions.

title: Spin-Adapted Neural-Network Backflow Wavefunctions for Excited States of Strongly Correlated Open-Shell Systems
abstract: Building on the success of neural-network quantum states (NQS) for molecular ground states, multi-state frameworks such as natural excited states (NES) [Pfau et al., Science 2024, 385, eadn0137] extend NQS to chemically important excited states. However, without control over total spin, such calculations can require the inclusion of many intervening states of other spins, particularly in strongly correlated systems with dense low-energy spectra. We therefore generalize our previously developed spin-adapted neural network backflow (SA-NNBF) ansatz [Li et al., arXiv:2604.06841 (2026)] to improve its variational flexibility for excited-state calculations within a prescribed spin sector. We establish the universality of this extended ansatz within the chosen orbital space and spin sector, and use numerical benchmarks to assess how parameter allocation affects the ansatz's accuracy. With the spin-adapted ansatz, we are able to directly optimize the first excited state (a singlet) of $O_2$ without using any multi-state frameworks. Combining the extended ansatz with NES, we obtain low-lying triplet states of $O_2$ and singlet states of the $[\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{S}_2(\mathrm{SCH}_3)_4]^{2-}$ cluster without including intervening states of other spins. Both the single-state and NES calculations achieve chemical accuracy relative to the exact energies. Our work provides a practical NQS framework for targeting excited states of prescribed spin in strongly correlated systems.

title: Spiroselenopyrans: Reversible Light- and Soft-Acid-Triggered Switching of Spirocyclic C–Se Bonds
abstract: Spiropyrans (SPs) are among the most exploited molecular scaffolds for photoswitching. Despite the potential of heavy chalcogen substitution at the spiro site to reshape bond characteristics and unlock distinct functionalities, SP analogs with chalcogens heavier than sulfur remain underexplored. Herein, we report the rational design and synthesis of spiroselenopyrans (SSPs), an emerging family of selenium-centered photoswitches, using steric hindrance engineering to suppress undesired benzoselenophene cyclization, a strategy that readily yields diversely substituted SSP derivatives.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Quadrature-Free Radial Intracule Densities: A Bessel-Harmonic Formulation for Gaussian Basis Sets
abstract: The radial intracule density $I(R)$, the probability distribution of the interelectronic distance, is a compact and physically transparent picture of electron correlation, but its evaluation for molecules has always relied on a numerical angular quadrature over the orientation of the interelectronic vector. We show that this quadrature can be removed altogether for Cartesian Gaussian basis sets and arbitrary second-order density matrices. Starting from the Hermite Gaussian expansion of the products of basis functions, the coupling exponential $e^{2μ\mathbf{R}\cdot\mathbf{T}}$ that links radial and angular variables is expanded in modified spherical Bessel functions and real spherical harmonics, and the expansion terminates rigorously at $l=p_x+p_y+p_z$, where the $p$'s are the Cartesian powers arising from the Hermite expansion. The angular average is then exact, the atomic limit reduces to a finite sum of terms $C_iR^{n_i}e^{-μR^2}$, and the radial moments $\int_0^\infty R^nI(R)\,dR$ are given in closed form through the confluent hypergeometric function ${}_1F_1$. The scheme is exact in principle and fails only arithmetically: we identify the catastrophic cancellations in the angular-momentum coupling that ruin binary64 evaluations for heavy atoms and remove them by elevating the cancelling chain to binary128. Sum rules for the total, Coulomb and exchange-correlation intracules are recovered to seven to eight significant digits for systems from LiH to Kr$_2$, whereas Euler-Maclaurin and Lebedev quadratures err by up to 22% for stretched or multicenter molecules.

title: Domain walls of a spin-chirality ferroelectric as tunable quantum particles
abstract: In frustrated spin chains with competing nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor exchange, the vector spin chirality sets the electric polarization, so a ferroelectric domain wall is a domain wall of the chirality. The semiclassical picture suggests nonlocal switching dynamics due to topological constraints on the spins, but little is known about such domain walls in a quantum spin chain. Using density-matrix renormalization group calculations for a frustrated spin-1/2 XXZ chain in which a bond alternation $δ$ opens a spin gap, we show that the wall then becomes a quantum particle. In a finite chain, it has the energy levels and wave functions of a particle in a box, and it moves under an electric field as a particle under a constant force does. In the infinite chain, its mass grows by more than two orders of magnitude as $δ$ decreases and diverges at $δ^*\approx0.012$, where the bottom of its band becomes flat; below $δ^*$ the band has two degenerate minima away from its center. The large mass results from a near cancellation of in-plane and out-of-plane exchange energies.

title: VQkit: A Unified and Extensible Framework for VASP and Quantum ESPRESSO Pre- and Post-Processing
abstract: VQkit is a Python-based computational toolkit developed to streamline the pre- and post-processing of density functional theory calculations performed using Vienna Ab initio Simulation Package (VASP) and Quantum ESPRESSO (QE). The framework employs a unified representation of lattice vectors, atomic coordinates, chemical species, and positional constraints, enabling cross-code structure conversion, geometry manipulation, crystallographic reconstruction, and code-specific input generation. Its pre-processing capabilities include symmetry-dependent reciprocal-space path generation, atomic constraints, and automated preparation of simulation inputs. The post-processing framework provides calculation convergence inspection, extraction of total energies and Fermi levels, electronic band-structure and density-of-states analysis, orbital-resolved electronic-structure processing, charge-density analysis, and evaluation of application-specific materials properties. The computational implementation is evaluated through elastic-property benchmarks for HfC, ZrC, ZrO2, Ti, and diamond, showing close agreement between VQkit and VASPKIT for VASP-based calculations, with differences observed in the corresponding QE results. By integrating cross-code interoperability, automated simulation preparation, standardized post-processing, and quantitative property evaluation within a common computational environment, VQkit reduces workflow fragmentation and facilitates consistent pre- and post-processing of first-principles calculations.

title: Computational Modeling of Sublattice Magnetization in CoTb/Co/CoTb Magnetic Multilayer Nanojunctions Between Cobalt Leads
abstract: In this work, we study the sublattice nano-magnetic behavior of CoTb/Co/CoTb sandwiched between semi-infinite cobalt leads. To perform the analysis, we use the Ising spin-based effective field theory (EFT), which enables us to determine the relevant magnetic exchange parameters for elemental cobalt JCo-Co and terbium JTb-Tb. The exchange interaction parameters are determined by fitting the magnetization calculated using the Ising effective-field theory to the experimentally measured temperature-dependent magnetization curves. This fitting procedure yields the exchange constants for Co and Tb, along with their respective Curie temperatures. We use the magnetic exchange parameter obtained using Ising EFT-based method is then seeded on to mean field theory (MFT) to calculate the sublattice magnetizations of CoTb/Co/CoTb arranged between semi-infinite cobalt leads. The sublattice magnetizations for every atomic layer and corresponding lattice sites in the layered ferrimagnetic nanostructures are computed separately. This allows us to analyze spin-site-specific parameters, magnetic moments, magnetization, and ferrimagnetic compensation behavior for varying eutectic compositions, particularly for \(c \leq 0.5\). The results give enhanced insight into magnetic phenomena at the local level and their general relevance in the ultra-thin layered ferrimagnetic structure dynamics confined between semi-infinite cobalt electrodes. These results are needed for the understanding of magnon transport phenomena and consequent magnetic amplification effects and are crucial to the development of spintronic technologies. Most importantly, to date, no first-principles or density functional theory research exists for sublattice magnetization in such multilayered systems. The versatile approach established in this work can also be applied to other nanostructured magnetic systems

title: Collisional lineshapes of an N$_2$-perturbed electronic transition in O$_2$ from first principles of quantum theory validated by accurate experimental spectra
abstract: We demonstrate the feasibility of predicting the lineshape of an electronic molecular transition collisionally perturbed by another molecule from first principles of quantum mechanics. We consider an N$_2$-perturbed O$_2$ $A$-band transition, which is relevant to spectroscopic observations in Earth's atmosphere. This approach simultaneously incorporates the electronic structure, quantum scattering and lineshape effects required to accurately predict pressure- and temperature-dependence of observed lineshapes. The $\textit{ab initio}$ lineshapes reproduce measurements to better than 0.6%. Theory also provides new physical constraints on beyond-Voigt lineshape parameters in fits of high-precision data, yielding fit residuals at the 0.08% level. This work motivates advances in molecular electronic structure calculations and demonstrates the potential to generate comprehensive spectroscopic reference data from first principles.

title: Prior-guided adaptive local refinement of foundation interatomic potentials
abstract: Foundation interatomic potentials enable simulations across diverse materials, but task-specific inaccuracies can require additional first-principles data. Obtaining these data is challenging when the relevant local environments arise in large simulation cells. Here we introduce the Prior-guided Adaptive Refinement Scheme (PARS), which identifies weakly supported environments during molecular dynamics by comparing their frozen representations with prototypes of pretraining environments, without requiring initial task labels or model ensembles. Selected environments are reconstructed as compact periodic cells for first-principles labelling and iterative refinement. Applications to phase stability, surface migration and vacancy clustering show improvements in target properties, including an 81% reduction in the mean absolute error of Ti vacancy-cluster energies per vacancy relative to the pretrained model. For Si/Ge, a foundation potential refined using 800 labelled cells containing 10-128 atoms is subsequently distilled into a compact potential without additional first-principles training labels. In simulations containing approximately 362,880 atoms, the distilled model predicts an interfacial thermal resistance consistent with that of a potential trained directly on density-functional theory data. These results demonstrate a route for adapting foundation potentials to target applications through local reference calculations.

title: What Do LLMs Use to Judge Synthesis Recipes? An Experimental Analysis on 240 Solid-State Syntheses
abstract: Inorganic materials discovery is increasingly limited by synthesis rather than by material design. Large language models (LLMs) are being adopted to propose synthesis conditions with little experimental evidence of their capabilities and biases. Here, we carry out an experimental synthesis benchmark of 240 experiments across eight known and unknown inorganic oxides and subsequently evaluate an LLM as a zero-shot ranker over fixed banks of solid-state synthesis recipes. For each pair of recipes for the same oxide target, `GPT-5.6-Sol` selects the recipe expected to yield higher target-phase purity. We aggregate these pairwise preferences using a regularized Bradley-Terry model to obtain a ranked list of synthesis recipes for a given target material. By comparison with the actual purity, obtained through X-ray diffraction, we measure `GPT-5.6-Sol`'s performance as a zero-shot ranker (0.72 pairwise accuracy). By selective removal of the information exposed to the model during this ranking, we conclude that ranking is driven predominantly by thermal features, with reaction chemistry modulating the effect. Ranking accuracy tracks the purity-temperature correlation by target (Spearman ρ= 0.91\), \(p = 0.002\), and on the six thermally-driven targets withholding all chemical identity hardly impacts performance (0.68) compared to withholding temperature (0.56). Ranking performance was higher on known than unknown targets, but the group-level difference was not statistically conclusive. The methodological choices highlight the need for more experimentally validated synthesis benchmarks and position LLMs as a thermally informed prior.

title: A Distributed Learning Framework for Energy-Aware Cooperative Navigation in Multi- Robot Systems
abstract: Cooperative Navigation Problem with Multiple Robots is known to be a quite challenging task, especially under unknown and dynamic traffic conditions. This happens since robots operating under these circumstances usually suffer from a lack of communication, inability to observe the whole environment, and a short lifetime due to a low level of available battery power. Traditional approaches to centralized control and planning for multi-robot navigation often fail here as they do not scale well and carry extremely large computational costs.

title: Koopmans spectral functionals for excitons in materials
abstract: Accurate first-principles characterization of excitons typically relies on the Bethe-Salpeter equation (BSE) combined with quasiparticle energies from computationally demanding GW calculations. Here, we replace the GW step with quasiparticle energies from Koopmans-compliant spectral functionals, an approach we call BSE@qKI, and implement it in an automated, reproducible AiiDA workflow. For a set of benchmark semiconductors, BSE@qKI reproduces experimental band gaps and first exciton energies with mean absolute relative errors of 13% and 4%, respectively, comparable to BSE@G0W0 for the gaps and markedly better for the excitation energies. We also apply the method to the layered magnetic semiconductor CrI3, obtaining an absorption spectrum that reproduces the main experimental features. These results establish BSE@qKI as a GW-free alternative to BSE@G0W0 for systematic studies of excitonic properties in complex materials.

title: Solvent/Antisolvent-Driven Etching of 2D Layered Halide Perovskite Microcrystals toward Endo-Epitaxial Heterostructures
abstract: Engineering internal interfaces within single crystals remains challenging, particularly in soft ionic materials such as layered halide perovskites (LHPs), for which conventional lithographic approaches are difficult to implement. Here we report a solvent/antisolvent-driven strategy for controlled etching of LHP microcrystals, producing well-defined rectangular cavities. Etching initiates at the top surface and proceeds preferentially along the crystallographic [100] and [010] directions. Cavity dimensions are tuned through etching time, temperature and etchant composition. The reaction can be interrupted and resumed, enabling stepwise cavity evolution through successive etching cycles. The resulting cavities serve as confined templates for regrowth of compositionally distinct LHPs, yielding endo-epitaxial heterostructures with designed internal architectures. The approach extends across diverse LHP compositions and antisolvent systems, while sequential precursor addition controls the extent of internal regrowth. This strategy establishes a route to engineering internal heterointerfaces in single-crystal perovskites through controlled chemical etching and confined growth.

title: Testing World Models on Actions They Have Never Seen: Held-Out Plans, Forecast Accuracy and Price Rules in Retail
abstract: A world model is trusted to answer "what if": how its world responds to an action it has never seen. We give a test of that trust for any action-conditioned world model: actions held out of training by design and scored against a known answer; whether forecast accuracy predicts accuracy on those actions; and the same structure given to simpler models. We run it in retail, where the action is a price and promotion plan, across 2,853 fitted models. First, forecast accuracy is a fair guide between kinds of model (rank correlation with error on new plans 0.32 to 0.66) and a poor guide between versions of one world model: where merchants plan into high-demand weeks the link reverses, down to -0.69. Second, training the world model to learn the effect of actions (JEPA pretraining, a latent consistency check, adaptation at the plan date) leaves its error on new plans unchanged. Third, in generated worlds the recorded regular price and three price rules improve it. Given the same rules, a log-linear model is best when its curve can match the truth; in a world whose curve lies outside the rules, the world model with the rules is ahead of the log-linear model with the rules in 36 of 40 worlds, and does as well without its recurrent cell. On real data (Breakfast at the Frat, The Complete Journey and M5) the rules lower the world model's error on pure price cuts deeper than any it saw (0.63 to 0.56 on the Frat; 0.45 to 0.44, within chance, on The Complete Journey), but not on lasting price moves. Fourth, a small share of random test plans helps every model a little. In a generated dosing world, a stress test in a second domain, the first finding repeats, and the built-up drug level lowers the world model's error (2.86 to 1.91) though it still predicts only 0.12 to 0.32 of the true gain. The test carries to any domain where a world model is asked about actions outside its history.

title: First-order correction to the self-consistent harmonic approximation free energy: Impact on the negative thermal expansion and phonon dynamics in ScF$_3$
abstract: Strongly anharmonic crystals are often treated using the self-consistent harmonic approximation with variationally optimized Gaussian density matrices or the related self-consistent phonon theory. Both approaches capture substantial phonon renormalization but exclude connected non-Gaussian free-energy correlations. Here, we derive the first-order post-variational correction generated by the lowest non-vanishing normal-ordered residual vertex. Normal ordering the residual interaction around the optimized state shows that the linear and quadratic vertices vanish at the stationary variational solution, leaving a fluctuation-dressed cubic interaction whose second-order vacuum and two-point contractions generate the free-energy correction and the dynamical bubble self-energy, respectively. In ScF$_3$, the variational optimization on the full Born-Oppenheimer potential accounts for most of the shift in the thermal-expansion crossover temperature between negative and positive values relative to self-consistent phonon theory with a fourth-order potential. The connected correction changes the crossover modestly, but its volume derivative appreciably shifts the pressure-remapped cubic local-stability limit. Using the bare cubic vertex appears to improve agreement with the thermodynamic measurements, yet it systematically underestimates the measured zone-boundary tilt-mode energies at high temperatures. The fluctuation-dressed interaction gives more moderate thermodynamic corrections but yields phonon energies in better agreement with experiments. These results show that connected non-Gaussian correlations can significantly affect free-energy derivatives and soft-mode dynamics near a structural instability, and identify the optimized Gaussian state as the natural reference for constructing residual interactions beyond the stochastic self-consistent harmonic approximation.

title: MillBill: A Machining Agent with Geometric Feedback
abstract: Turning a CAD model into a machining program requires both process knowledge and geometric precision. Language models can generate such workflows by writing geometry and toolpath code for each part, but this makes numerical execution part of the model's task. We introduce MillBill, an agent that separates machining decisions from their geometric execution and verification. Given a boundary-representation part, stock, and material, a locally hosted, mid-sized open model proposes operations and cutting parameters for indexed three-axis machining. A geometric harness generates toolpaths, simulates material removal, and returns feedback for plan refinement. Setup planning accounts for what the available cutters can physically reach, rather than visibility alone. We evaluate the resulting programs by the fraction of the target surface area within the specified tolerance after simulated machining. With Qwen3.8-27B, MillBill outperforms frontier-model approaches that construct their own geometry and toolpath workflows on the evaluated machining tasks. Code: https://github.com/kulibinai/millbill

title: Targeted material doping to enable the formation and coherent propagation of Laser Induced Periodic Surface Structures (LIPSS): the ZnO paradigm
abstract: This work explores how the initial free carrier density governs the formation and coherent propagation of Low Spatial Frequency Laser-Induced Periodic Surface Structures (LSF-LIPSS). As a paradigm we have analyzed the behavior of ad-hoc-doped ZnO films. ZnO is a multifunctional Transparent Conducting Oxide (TCO) with many scientific and technologic uses including applications in biomedicine, photonics, sensing or photocatalysis. Many of them would benefit from the use of large area, electrically anisotropic surfaces. By introducing small amounts of Yb3+ as donor dopant in ZnO films grown by Pulse Laser Deposition (PLD), we have substantially improved its carrier density at room temperature (RT) and its electrical conductivity while preserving the functional properties of pure ZnO. For RT carrier densities ne > 1019 cm-3, coherent propagation of LSF-LIPSS has been successfully achieved upon irradiation with 350 fs laser pulses at 1030 nm at high repetition rate (500 kHz) and for laser scanning speeds well above 1 m/s. However, the ablation mechanism (ZnO sublimation at the LIPSS valleys) and the large melting temperature of ZnO, make the thermal conductivity of the substrate, the film thickness and the irradiation pulse duration to play a crucial role in determining the morphology of the LSF-LIPPS propagated over large areas, especially in avoiding film cracking. The results achieved upon optimization fully confirm the role of free carrier density in the large-scale propagation of high quality LSF-LIPSS in doped ZnO and enable using these structures to easily generate large electrical anisotropies over macroscopic regions with conductivities along the LIPSS several times larger than transversally.

title: Adaptive LLM-Driven Honeypots vs. LLM-Driven Attackers: Does Narrative Coherence Improve Deception?
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) enable honeypots to generate responses and deceptive artefacts on demand, yet existing approaches evaluate generated content one reply at a time and leave open whether artefacts that jointly describe a coherent event retain an attacker better than unrelated ones. This question becomes pressing as autonomous LLM-driven offensive agents emerge as realistic adversaries. This paper proposes narrative deception, a reactive strategy in which the defender maps each observed attacker command to a MITRE ATT&CK technique, selects a compatible scenario from a curated catalogue based on MITRE Engage, and deploys mutually referential artefacts (files, processes, services, and logs) on an emulated Ubuntu host while the intrusion is under way. An LLM-powered defender and an autonomous LLM attacker interact through a real SSH session, and the attacker's termination policy distinguishes abandonment due to suspected deception from abandonment due to loss of interest. A campaign of 1,150 sessions compares four conditions of increasing sophistication (Static, Same-TTP, Multi-TTP, and Chain) across four open-weight attacker models, four defender models, and three attacker skill levels. Engagement increases significantly at every step. With the same artefact budget per reaction, coherent scenarios raise the median session length of advanced attackers from 40 to 165 commands and reduce their abandonment from 86% to 52%. The effect grows with attacker skill, holds across all sixteen model pairs, and comes at comparable inference cost. Nearly all sessions ended through loss of interest rather than detection, which suggests that deception should sustain meaningful findings, not only emulator fidelity.

title: Magnetic History and Field Sweep Rate Effects on Transformation Hysteresis in $\mathrm{Ni}_{41}\mathrm{Co}_{9}\mathrm{Mn}_{31.5}\mathrm{Ga}_{18.5}$
abstract: Hysteresis in magnetic-field-induced structural phase transformations is a major obstacle to the application of metamagnetic shape memory alloys. One promising approach to reduce hysteresis is to utilize a metastable martensitic state generated by magnetic-field cycling. However, the mechanism by which the metastable state reduces hysteresis remains unclear. Here, microsecond pulsed-field magnetization measurements are used to investigate the transformation kinetics of $\mathrm{Ni}_{41}\mathrm{Co}_{9}\mathrm{Mn}_{31.5}\mathrm{Ga}_{18.5}$. Magnetic-field cycling reduces the hysteresis width by approximately 50-60%, demonstrating that substantial suppression persists on a microsecond timescale. Comparison with millisecond pulsed-field measurements suggests that the reverse martensitic transformation field is more sensitive to the field sweep rate for the metastable martensite than for the initial martensite. Possible explanations include enhanced thermal activation associated with a lower effective activation barrier and differences in the athermal contribution arising from different metastable martensitic microstructures.

title: Efficient Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
abstract: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) reach an accuracy close to quantum mechanical reference calculations at a small fraction of the cost. Efficiency is the purpose of MLIPs, yet strategies for efficient MLIPs have not been reviewed systematically. This review takes efficiency as its guideline. To compare MLIPs on a common footing, we represent them in a complete basis expansion, the Atomic Cluster Expansion (ACE) and its graph generalization (GRACE). The expansion is canonical, built from products of single-particle functions. Classical interatomic potentials, such as the embedded-atom method, and many modern MLIPs, including equivariant transformers, can be represented within this expansion. Much of the apparent diversity of MLIP architectures therefore reflects how non-linearity, layer coupling and optimization are handled rather than which interactions the models can represent. We show how the cost of an MLIP becomes linear in system size and, at fixed rank of the tensor decomposition, in model complexity, and we discuss the role of machine learning, which provides non-linear parameterizations and optimization. Because efficiency is meaningful only at a given accuracy, we also compare accuracy and cost. On the Matbench Discovery leaderboard, models with three to five layers approach the accuracy of deeper models, and one basis, truncated along the Pareto front of error and speed, spans more than two orders of magnitude in cost. Ultimately, training data determine the quality of any MLIP.

title: Orbital differentiation in a rare earth ion near half filling
abstract: In the electronic structure of rare earth ions, details can be crucial for understanding the origin of correlated states. Currently, state-of-the-art wavefunction-based methods (e.g. CASSCF) can capture single-ion properties of molecular magnets and some band insulating systems, but are expensive to perform, and cannot be applied to metallic systems. Here, we carry out full multiplet calculations for SmN with the cubic rock-salt structure using the crystal field software Quanty. The calculated experimental observables from our model agree precisely with magnetic susceptibility and inelastic neutron scattering experiments, and the spatially resolved spin density also agrees with DFT predictions. By tuning the crystal field parameters, our full multiplet-derived wavefunctions reveal the presence of orbital differentiation of the ground $J=\frac{5}{2}$ manifold into two groups, which are distinct subspaces with different orbital stiffness. This violation of Hund's rule, observed with a fast and inexpensive calculation tool, represents a step forward for microscopic models of rare earth materials, and may provide support for the claim of unconventional triplet superconductivity in SmN.

title: Assessment of electric-field-induced forces for bulk solids within the projector-augmented wave method
abstract: We assess the performance of electric-field-induced forces for bulk solids within the projector-augmented wave method. This capability allows for first-principles structural relaxations of bulk semiconductors and insulators under external electric fields, thereby enabling the calculation of linear and nonlinear responses to electric fields as well as properties associated with electric-field-driven structural changes. The approach is first validated by presenting calculated ion-clamped and unclamped dielectric and piezoelectric constants, quadratic dielectric susceptibilities, and Born effective charges for semiconductors AlX (X=P, As and Sb), showing good agreement with density functional perturbation theory calculations as well as with available experimental and theoretical data. As a further demonstration, we examine the electric-field-driven antiferroelectric-to-ferroelectric phase transition in AgNbO$_3$, for which our computed polarization versus electric field hysteresis loop aligns with previous calculations.

title: SciWorkBench: A Benchmark for Real Scientific Workflows
abstract: Language models are increasingly being used as agents capable of planning and executing projects, as well as refining their actions through feedback. This shift raises a question: can current agents complete projects like real scientists? To examine this question, we introduce SciWorkBench, a benchmark for evaluating agents' abilities on real science tasks across biology, chemistry, materials science, and physics. SciWorkBench is built from peer-reviewed literature or expert-contributed research scenarios. We also propose a unified scientific analysis framework validated by domain experts, which can categorize most tasks in SciWorkBench. Each task covers one or more stages of this framework. We evaluate up-to-date models within the Claude Code and Codex agent frameworks under a unified execution and grading protocol. The best-performing agent achieves a mean score of 57.38, indicating that current agents still struggle with realistic scientific workflows. Our failure analysis identifies three recurring weaknesses at the workflow level: difficulty translating scientific knowledge into task-specific procedures, weak integration of evidence across different modalities, and limited capacity for scientific self-correction. These findings highlight the importance of workflow-based evaluation for measuring progress toward reliable AI systems for scientific research.

title: Combined magnetic and structural transition state in first-principles calculations
abstract: We present a generalized nudged elastic band (NEB) implementation within potential-based constrained density-functional theory (cDFT) for calculating transition pathways that simultaneously optimize atomic, lattice, and magnetic degrees of freedom. Unlike standard fixed-cell NEB calculations restricted to atomic displacements, our framework consistently couples atomic forces, stresses, and spin torques. The method supports fixed- and variable-cell approaches for collinear and non- collinear magnetic configurations, by incorporating magnetic torques and generalized cell coordinates within the NEB optimization. To validate the methodology, we present benchmark calculations for representative magnetostructural systems. Specifically, we investigate the bcc-to-hcp transformation in Fe and the antiferromagnetic-to-ferromagnetic transition in FeRh using the variable-cell formalism. Furthermore, we examine spin-reversal processes in two-dimensional CrI3 to analyze the influence of spin-orbit coupling on transition paths and their associated energy barriers.

title: Burgers vectors from Voronoi topology
abstract: Automated dislocation analysis is standard in atomistic simulations, yet current tools are limited to a handful of crystal structures. We introduce an algorithm without adjustable parameters, based on Voronoi topology, that identifies dislocations in a broad class of crystals. Each face shared by two cells that match the ideal crystal is taken as a step in it, and summing these steps around closed circuits of such cells yields exact Burgers vectors, without geometric templates. Tested on dislocations inserted into all 9,610 Materials Project structures whose Voronoi cells are stable with a wide margin, the algorithm finds every dislocation with its correct Burgers vector. In raw molecular-dynamics snapshots, including eleven dislocation types in $θ$-Al$_2$Cu and bcc iron up to its melting point, every Burgers vector it returns is correct, although near melting the dislocations merge into one cluster. Voronoi topology thus provides a natural language in which a crystal, its defects, and their Burgers vectors are all described.

title: Tailoring Spin-Crossover Transitions in Fe(HB(tz)3)2 via Cocrystallization for Low-Temperature Barocaloric Cooling
abstract: Spin-crossover (SCO) phase transitions can drive large barocaloric effects─thermal changes induced by applied hydrostatic pressure that enable heat to be moved against a temperature gradient. Although several SCO compounds have been reported to display promising barocaloric properties─including high pressure sensitivity, a large entropy change, and minimal transition hysteresis─it is challenging to control the transition temperature of a material without adversely impacting its phase-change behavior. This limitation restricts the scope of thermal applications relevant to a given SCO material.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Sulfurization Breaking the Ferroelectric Polarization Bottleneck in PbTiO3
abstract: Robust ferroelectricity is crucial for high-performance ferroelectric nonvolatile memories. PbTiO3 (PTO) is expected to show large polarization with a high Curie temperature (TC). However, the inherent leakage current of PTO limits its actual ferroelectricity. To address this limitation, we prepare PTO films via sulfurization using a cost-effective sol–gel method. The pristine PTO films show notable remnant polarization (Pr) of 61.6 μC/cm2 with well-saturated electric field–polarization loops that have not been achieved in either bulk or thin-film forms previously.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Electrocatalytic Conversion of Diethylene Glycol into Diglycolic Acid by Promoted Ni2+/Ni3+ Redox
abstract: Diethylene glycol (DEG), a major byproduct generated during industrial ethylene glycol synthesis via ethylene route, possesses potential for value upgrading. Herein, an electrocatalytic conversion route of DEG to diglycolic acid (DGA) has been demonstrated and the reaction mechanism has been explored in-depth. Typically, a Cr-Ni(OH)2/NF (Ni foam) electrocatalyst was synthesized, achieving a Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 90.88% and a selectivity of 90.73% in three-electrode configuration.

title: Small-Molecule Activation Reshapes the Catalytic Conformational Landscape during Ca2+ ATPase Turnover
abstract: Understanding how small molecules enhance enzymatic turnover is a central challenge in chemical biology because activation arises from redistribution of transient populations that are difficult to resolve during catalysis. By integrating time-resolved X-ray solution scattering, molecular dynamics simulations, and kinetic modeling, we determine how the small-molecule activator yakuchinone A modulates the catalytic cycle of the sarco/endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ ATPase (SERCA), a prototypical P-type ATPase. We show that the activator accelerates the catalytic cycle by reshaping the conformational landscape during turnover, with a disproportionate enhancement of late-cycle transitions. This kinetic modulation of the rate-limiting step increases the population of Ca2+-bound E2P states, while significantly reducing accumulation of Ca2+-free E2*Pi transient states associated with dephosphorylation. Ensemble-based structural models quantitatively reproduce the experimental scattering profiles and support redistribution of conformational populations during turnover. Together, these findings provide a time-resolved mechanistic picture of how small molecules enhance enzymatic turnover through redistribution of conformational populations and selective acceleration of rate-limiting transitions.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Artificial intelligence-based finish-line detection and margin-related accuracy in fixed prosthodontic digital workflows: A systematic review and functional meta-synthesis
abstract: Statement of problemArtificial intelligence (AI) has been increasingly incorporated into fixed prosthodontic digital workflows, but evidence regarding finish-line detection, margin handling, and margin-related crown accuracy remains heterogeneous.PurposeThe purpose of this systematic review was to evaluate AI-based finish-line detection, margin-line extraction, and margin-related accuracy in tooth-supported fixed prosthodontic workflows using a functional meta-synthesis.Material and methodsThe PubMed, Scopus, and Embase databases were searched through May 2026.

title: Optical Spectroscopy and Machine Learning for Skin Cancer Detection: Why Cohort Size, Validation Rigor and Calibration - Not Architecture - Govern Clinical Readiness
abstract: Optical vibrational spectroscopy - principally Raman, with near-infrared (NIR) reflectance as a lower-cost proxy - combined with machine learning has been proposed as a non-invasive skin cancer triage adjunct, yet the field remains dominated by small single-centre cohorts and by deep networks reported without a matched classical baseline or leakage-free validation. The objective of this study is to determine whether architecture or methodology governs clinical readiness in this data regime.
venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine

title: Multitime Scale Operando Kinetic Decoupling of Photogenerated Carriers
abstract: The energy-conversion efficiency of photoelectrochemical (PEC) systems is governed by photogenerated charge-carrier kinetics that span several orders of magnitude, from subpicosecond generation in the semiconductor bulk to millisecond consumption at catalytic surfaces. This vast temporal disparity severs the causal link between ultrafast carrier events and steady-state photocurrents, leaving the mechanistic origins of efficiency losses speculative and fundamentally hindering the rational optimization of PEC devices.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: A Nanoscale Valley Sink Governs Temperature-Dependent Catalytic Selectivity on Corrugated Iron Carbide
abstract: Predicting reaction selectivity on corrugated catalytic interfaces remains a major challenge when observed pathway bifurcations cannot be rationalized by static, single-site activation barriers alone. Here, by coupling neural-network-accelerated gas–solid nanoreactor molecular dynamics (GS-NMD) with first-principles calculations and microkinetic modeling, we elucidate the atomistic origin of the temperature-dependent ethylene polymerization switch on corrugated Fe3C(102).

title: Discovery of new antiviral agents through artificial intelligence: in vitro and in vivo results
abstract: In this research, we employed a deep reinforcement learning (RL)-based molecule design platform to generate a diverse set of compounds targeting the neuraminidase (NA) of influenza A and B viruses. A total of 60291 compounds were generated, of which 86.5% displayed superior physicochemical properties compared to oseltamivir. After narrowing down the selection through computational filters, nine compounds with non-sialic acid-like structures were selected for in vitro experiments. We identified two compounds, DS-22-inf-009 and DS-22-inf-021 that effectively inhibited the NAs of both influenza A and B viruses (IAV and IBV), including H275Y mutant strains at low micromolar concentrations. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed a similar pattern of interaction with amino acid residues as oseltamivir. In cell-based assays, DS-22-inf-009 and DS-22-inf-021 inhibited IAV and IBV in a dose-dependent manner with EC50 values ranging from 0.29 uM to 2.31 uM. Furthermore, animal experiments showed that both DS-22-inf-009 and DS-22-inf-021 exerted antiviral activity in mice, conferring 65% and 85% protection from IAV (H1N1 pdm09), and 65% and 100% protection from IBV (Yamagata lineage), respectively. Thus, these findings demonstrate the potential of RL to generate compounds with promising antiviral properties.

title: Beyond animal testing: integrated AI-PBPK-MPS framework for human-relevant toxicology
abstract: NAMs are revolutionizing safety assessment and bridging the substantial disconnect between traditional animal toxicology studies and human exposure within the pharmaceutical industry. AI predictive toxicology uses graph neural networks, deep learning, explainable AI, PBPK, and IVIVE modeling for human-dose predictions, and micro-physiological and organ-on-a-chip systems that replicate specific physiological states.

title: An engineered probiotic with integrated biocomputation and multi-molecular recording for precision theranostics of colitis
abstract: Engineered therapeutic microbes capable of sensing and responding to diseases offer transformative potential for precision medicine. However, their capacity to intelligently process the complex and dynamic biomarkers of multifaceted diseases such as inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) remains limited. Here, we design a probiotic system that executes logic computations through four stage-specific inflammatory biomarkers, enabling precise diagnosis and closed-loop treatment of colitis in mice. Integration with a CRISPR-based molecular recorder allows dynamic tracking of biomarker levels and converts inflammatory signals into quantifiable, site-specific base-editing events, thereby achieving precise diagnosis and analysis of disease progression within a living mammalian gut. We additionally develop a multimodal machine-learning classifier that utilizes both bioluminescent reporter signals and sequencing data to accurately stage intestinal inflammation with an accuracy of 0.83 ± 0.05. Together, this work provides a robust platform for in situ biocomputation and marks a significant advance toward intelligent, precision theranostics for gastrointestinal disorders.

title: Bandedge-State-Limited Single-Photon Emission from Volumetric Quantum Design of 2D Colloidal Quantum Wells
abstract: Present-day solution-processable single-photon sources are dominated by three-dimensionally confined colloidal quantum emitters, yet their particle-to-particle variation in single-exciton properties limits reproducibility and scalability. Here, to avoid such heterogeneity, we demonstrate reliable room-temperature single-photon emission from atomically flat two-dimensional (2D) colloidal quantum wells (CQWs) with inherently uniform one-dimensional quantum confinement, despite their long-standing limitations of efficient multiexciton emission and pronounced exciton-surface susceptibility. We resolve these challenges through volumetric quantum design (VQD) of CQWs, yielding a highly localized, single bandedge state. This design laterally confines the bandedge excitonic domain within the exciton coherent area and vertically decouples it from surface states via a thick, strain-relieved quantum-barrier shell that preserves strong confinement, overcoming the daunting thickness-confinement trade-off in 2D CQWs. Statistical single-particle spectroscopy reveals that VQD-CQWs deliver near-blinking-free (on-time: >99.5%) and fluence-insensitive antibunching (g(2)(0): ∼0.041), protected by a bandedge-state-filling bottleneck, together with linear polarization of up to 73% under cavity-free conditions, originating from synergistic transition-dipole and electric-field anisotropies. These advances establish 2D CQWs as a viable, homogeneous and scalable platform for quantum technologies.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Mapping the Evolution of Digital Health Innovation Using an Agentic AI-Assisted Longitudinal Horizon-Scanning Methodology
abstract: Background: Increasing volumes of heterogeneous digital-health intelligence challenge conventional horizon-scanning methods and their ability to examine how technologies, clinical priorities and innovation pathways evolve over time. This study developed an agentic AI-assisted methodology for longitudinal digital-health horizon scanning. Methods: We analysed 123 NHS horizon scans conducted in 2015 and annually from 2019 to 2026, comprising 4,039 company-year profiles. Horizon-scan records were integrated with policy, clinical, funding and media evidence.

title: Pair distribution function oscillations at electrostatically stabilized nanocrystal surfaces reflect nanocrystal lattice periodicity
abstract: Nanocrystals (NCs) stabilized electrostatically by short, multivalent inorganic ligands exhibit rich interactions and phase behavior believed to hinge on the configuration of ions at the NC surface, yet these molecular details have not previously been measured. Here we use double-difference pair distribution functions (ddPDFs) of total X-ray scattering to determine the configuration of Sn$_2$S$_6^{4-}$ ligands on PbS NCs suspended in multivalent electrolyte. The measured ddPDFs exhibit a $\sim$3-$\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$ wavelength oscillation that extends $\sim$10 $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$. Comparison with a PbS NC model decorated with Sn$_2$S$_6^{4-}$ ligands indicates ligands are aligned $\sim$radially, suggesting bidentate binding. Calculated partial PDFs show that the oscillatory signal is dominated by nanocrystal-Pb to ligand-Sn correlations. A simplified model that replaces the ligand with a strongly scattering Pt atom near the NC surface confirms the oscillation period in the ddPDF originates from the NC lattice constant. Nanocrystal lattice periodicity therefore merits consideration when interpreting ddPDFs of colloidal NCs.

title: Sobolev theory for the inverse problem of time-dependent density functional theory on the torus
abstract: We show that, given a sufficiently regular time-dependent density, there exists a unique potential such that the Schrödinger equation with this external potential has the prescribed one-particle density. We treat densities that are twice differentiable in time and of finite Sobolev regularity in space; the resulting potentials are continuous in time and of finite Sobolev regularity in space. Our method of proof is to rewrite the problem as a nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a loss of derivatives, which we in turn handle with a completion-of-the-square argument. This is a refinement of our recent work [Lauritsen, Lewin, and Oldenburg, arXiv:2609.08984], which handled this loss of derivatives using the Cauchy-Kovalevskaya theorem and treated analytic-in-space densities and potentials.

title: A Molecular Glue that Regulates Processing of Non-Coding RNAs in Human Cells
abstract: Small nuclear RNAs (snRNAs) are a major class of non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) and essential components of the spliceosome. Chemical tools for perturbing snRNA structure and function are lacking, and ncRNAs have more generally been considered undruggable. Here we use chemical proteomics and cryo-electron microscopy to identify a covalent molecular glue HL-1B that stabilizes binding of the 3'-exonuclease TOE1 to the spliceosome in a catalytically competent state. We show that HL-1B triggers excess 3'-processing of snRNAs in human cells that is tunable by the expression levels of TOE1 and auxiliary splicing regulators like SNRPB2, which, in turn, create synthetic lethality interactions with HL-1B that correlate with the preferential modulation of intermediate exon inclusion splicing events. Our findings reveal a fundamental role for snRNA tail length in regulating spliceosome function and, more generally, a way to target ncRNAs with non-orthosteric small molecules that remodel the interactomes of RNA processing enzymes in cells.

title: Rapid screening of target-specific isotope labeling protocols for in situ NMR of bacterial membrane proteins
abstract: We describe an approach for the efficient development of targeted isotope labeling protocols leading to nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) structural studies of bacterial membrane proteins in intact cells and native outer membrane (OM) vesicles (OMVs). The assay relies on the bioorthogonal non-canonical amino acid tagging (BONCAT) approach for metabolic incorporation of an azide-bearing residue, followed by copper-catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC) to an alkyne-functionalized fluorescent dye. Fluorescence detection in SDS-PAGE provides a rapid way to test samples for off-target background signal from endogenous proteins, bypassing the need for intensive NMR screening experiments. Using this approach, we develop an optimized protocol that enables high-resolution NMR spectra to be obtained in situ with negligible background signal. The BONCAT approach also enables target-specific fluorescence or nano-gold labeling of proteins at the OM surface, further extending the utility of this protocol for correlative structure-activity studies of membrane proteins in situ.

title: From quasiperiodic three-colour order on a triangular lattice to covalent carbon sheets
abstract: Can the quasiperiodic colouring of a lattice be encoded in the bonds of a single carbon sheet? We construct golden-, silver- and bronze-mean three-colour patterns on a triangular lattice. The positions of one colour determine the other two through a nearest-neighbour rule. The three patterns have eight, nine and seven first-shell environments, respectively. A triangle of three identical motifs frustrates the alternating bond ports of each of the three molecular alphabets in the golden and silver patterns. The bronze pattern admits four designs with direct or ethynylene connections. Three periodic structures reproduce its infinite environment frequencies in a local-energy model. For a 708-atom sheet with independently matched environment counts, the predicted energy lies 0.295 meV per carbon below the density-functional result. Across four periodic cells initialized from two smaller donors, relaxation changes the bond lengths by at most 0.00113 angstroms in root-mean-square terms. Fitting one 60-degree sector to relaxed periodic geometries gives complete sixfold-symmetric fragments with up to 22,140 carbon atoms. In the 13,950-atom directly linked sheet, a $π$ doublet places 79.05% of its weight in a boundary shell comprising 7.96% of the atoms, whereas the lowest unoccupied doublet places only 0.124% there. These calculations connect a testable motif-selection rule to the energetics and finite-patch spectra of candidate quasiperiodic carbon sheets.

title: Electrical addressing of compensated magnetic order in artificial spin ice
abstract: Compensated magnetic systems, such as antiferromagnets, hold immense potential for spintronic devices thanks to vanishing stray fields, robustness to perturbations, and ultrafast dynamics. Yet, electrical writing and reading of their order remains a major challenge. Here we use artificial spin ice as a mesoscale platform in which compensated order can be engineered, directly imaged, and electrically controlled. Specifically, we demonstrate combined electrical writing and reading of a compensated state in a triangular artificial spin ice. Exploiting the orientation dependence of the spin-orbit torque switching current, we independently switch three nanomagnet sublattices through a single current channel, with the planar Hall effect providing sublattice-resolved readout. This grants access to all eight magnetization states of the triangular plaquette, including its fully compensated state, yielding a nonlinear, history-dependent electrical response. Our results establish an approach to electrically programmable compensated magnetic systems and provide an important foundation for reconfigurable magnetic devices and unconventional computing.

title: Seeing the Unseen: Sensitivity, Reporting Vocabulary, and Translation Barriers in Optical and Magnetoplasmonic Biosensing
abstract: Three decades of progress in light–matter interaction at metal–dielectric interfaces have pushed optical biosensor detection limits from the micromolar to the femtomolar range and below, yet the translation of this sensitivity into devices that perform reliably in clinical, environmental, and industrial samples has lagged far behind. This review argues that buffer-phase sensitivity is no longer the limiting quantity.
