title: Development of a Temperature-Based Method for Repeated Markerless Gene Integration in cyanobacterium Synechococcus elongatus PCC 7942
abstract: Genetic engineering of cyanobacteria can require multiple rounds of genome modification, highlighting the need for flexible markerless engineering tools. Here, we established a temperature-based markerless gene integration method using the temperature-sensitive H1 strain of Synechococcus elongatus PCC 7942, which, unlike the wild-type strain, cannot grow at 40 {degrees}C. Disruption of nynA, encoding a putative endoribonuclease, allowed H1 to grow at 40 {degrees}C, enabling transformants with genes integrated at the nynA locus to be selected without an antibiotic-resistance marker. Complementation of nynA at a separate genomic locus restored temperature sensitivity, allowing the same selection principle to be reused. Using this strategy, gfp, mScarlet, and luciferase were sequentially integrated, with all three genes retained and expressed. To demonstrate its applicability to metabolic engineering, markerless integration of cnsA, encoding cineole synthase, enabled 1,8-cineole production at 81.4 {+/-} 9.52 {micro}g /g wet cell weight. This strategy enables repeated markerless genome modification in the H1 strain using temperature-based selection.

title: FluoMALDI Imaging: An Integrated Multimodality Platform for Biologically Informed Spatial-Omics
abstract: FluoMALDI imaging integrates fluorescence microscopy and matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry imaging (MALDI-MSI) of tissues and cells, leveraging matrix-enhanced fluorescence signals to enable spatially guided functional molecular discovery. Here we report three broadly applicable FluoMALDI paradigms that link how genes, proteins, and organelles shape spatial molecular composition. These advances are achieved by integrating immuno-, HaloTag-, and dye-based labels into a unified FluoMALDI imaging framework.

title: A Lanthanide-Containing PQQ-Dependent Enzyme with Broad Substrate Scope for Sugars, Alcohols, and Aldehydes
abstract: Since the discovery of lanthanide-containing methanol dehydrogenases (Ln-MDHs), lanthanide (Ln) biochemistry has undergone a notable shift, revealing a class of pyrroloquinoline quinone (PQQ)-dependent oxidoreductases that specifically utilize Ln ions (Ln3+) as cofactors. A few Ln-containing alcohol dehydrogenases have been reported to oxidize a broad range of substrates, including primary and secondary alcohols as well as aldehydes. This suggests the existence of enzymes with broader substrate scopes than previously anticipated.

title: Molecular energies from sparse quantum prolate diagonalization on a trapped-ion quantum processor
abstract: We introduce sparse quantum prolate diagonalization (sparse QPD), which combines the original formulation of QPD [Phys. Rev. Res., 8(3), 033177, (2026)] with compressed sensing to exploit Hamiltonian spectrum sparsity for molecular systems. We show that sparse sampling reduces the sample complexity of QPD from $\mathcal{O}(N_s)$ to $\mathcal{O}(\log N_s)$, where $N_s$ is the number of sampled points of the autocorrelation function (i.e.\ distinct circuits), without increasing circuit depth at chemical accuracy. With a two-orbital active-space-embedded Hamiltonian for an interacting arginine--tryptophan residue pair in water as an example, we show that on the Quantinuum Helios trapped-ion quantum computer, sparse QPD resolves the Hamiltonian energies to chemical accuracy with circuits of up to 448 two-qubit gates. For a suitably large quantum processor, we demonstrate numerically in the weakly correlated regime that the method extends to larger systems.

title: Mechanically induced self-propagating reactions within the realm of mechanochemistry: Fundamentals, overview, in situ monitoring and perspectives
abstract: Mechanically induced self-propagating reaction (MSR) represents a promising but rather underexplored phenomenon within mechanochemistry, a solvent-free alternative to classical solution-based chemistry. In contrast to the gradual mechanochemical reactions, MSRs are sub-second combustive-like processes bringing about substantial benefits such as faster product formation, time efficiency, and lower energy consumption. Despite the fact that the mechanochemical field is in the research spotlight, MSR investigation remains on the periphery. This review aims to catalyze a renaissance in MSR fundamentals investigation by reviewing the current state-of-the-art. This is done via systematically reviewing the reaction systems that were reported to react via a MSR in the past twenty years, such as metal-metalloid ones (carbides, borides, silicides, and carbonitrides), metal chalcogenides, metal oxides, and other specific types of reactions. A couple of case studies are briefly reviewed for each system, and the comprehensive table follows afterward. The review also revisits the factors impacting the MSR course from milling conditions and reagent's properties point of view, showing either a direct or inverse relationship with MSR ignition time. The recent development in the in situ monitoring of mechanochemical reactions allowed to obtain some mechanistic insights into the MSR process, which are summarized in the last chapter.

title: Temperature Flips the Sign of the Hydrogen Response in Nanogranular Palladium Networks
abstract: In nanogranular palladium networks, hydrogen uptake has two opposing effects on electrical resistance. Absorbed hydrogen scatters electrons within the particles, raising their resistance, while particle expansion narrows the gaps between them and lowers the junction resistance. Such networks are widely studied as resistive hydrogen sensors, and the sign of their net response is usually treated as a fixed property of the architecture. In networks grown by atomic layer deposition on macroporous silicon, we show that changing the operating temperature can reverse this sign at a fixed hydrogen concentration. A thermodynamic model indicates that scattering contributes less as temperature rises, allowing sub-angstroem changes in gap width to dominate. Where the two effects cancel, the network absorbs hydrogen yet gives the same reading as in hydrogen-free gas, so a leak could escape detection. Between 25 and 40 degrees Celsius, this cancellation point is predicted to rise over tenfold, crossing reported leak-alarm setpoints. At 55 degrees Celsius, the measured response stays negative but passes through a minimum, so a concentration above a setpoint can mimic one below it. Annealing at 200 degrees Celsius alters the calibration and turns the room-temperature response negative at the lowest concentration tested. Quantitative sensing therefore requires a defined thermal pretreatment and an operating temperature giving distinct signals across the intended concentration range. Response polarity becomes an operating parameter rather than a fixed property. More broadly, any nanoparticle network whose particles deform on sorption may show the same temperature-dependent competition between transport within and between particles, with implications for sensors and switches beyond palladium-hydrogen.

title: Engineering third order absorbing exceptional points in multi-drive cavity magnonics for enhanced sensing
abstract: We consider a four mode cavity magnonics system consisting of two coupled resonators containing a pair of YIG spheres. Each resonator has two input-output ports allowing for the application of multiple drive fields. We show that with control of the dipolar coupling strength between the YIG spheres the relative amplitude and phase of the drive fields can be used to tune the system to third order absorbing exceptional points. The system considered here offers considerable flexibility and may be useful for high sensitivity detection as absorbing exceptional points can avoid the eigenbasis collapse associated with their resonant counterparts.

title: Engineering antiferromagnetic (LaVO3)m/(PrVO3)n superlattices
abstract: In this study, we demonstrate the atomic-scale engineering of antiferromagnetic (LaVO3)m/(PrVO3)n superlattices grown by MBE on (001)-oriented SrTiO3 substrates. Our work achieved a precise layer-by-layer control, revealing how interface-driven structural distortions can be systematically tuned. X-ray diffraction and reciprocal space mapping confirm both the epitaxial strain state and the high crystalline quality of the superlattices. High-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy further uncovers layer-resolved atomic displacements, where La3+ and Pr3+ exhibit antipolar motions modulated by the superlattice periodicity. The alternate stackings of LaVO3 and PrVO3 yield a unique antiferromagnetic transition temperature, which can be tuned by adjusting their relative proportions. This behavior exists despite the distinct spin ordering temperatures observed in the constituent materials. Layer-resolved spectroscopic measurements reveal that the hybridization of La and Pr 5d orbitals with O 2p orbitals is also modulated and directly correlated to the oxygen octahedra rotations. By determining the orbital hybridization and mapping the cation displacements as proxies, we can visualize indirectly the trilinear coupling between oxygen octahedra rotations and antipolar rare earth displacements. Notably, the interfacial oxygen octahedra connectivity between cubic SrTiO3 substrate and orthorhombic vanadate layers significantly influences the structural distortions. These distortions, almost quenched near the interface, relax over few unit cells, demonstrating how strain and interfacial effects propagate through the superlattice. This study illustrates how artificial superlattices can be engineered to control structural distortions at the atomic scale, offering a pathway to tune the magnetic properties through strain-distortion relationships in perovskite oxides.

title: Born for the Task: Rethinking Quantum Chemistry with Foresighted Agentic Computing
abstract: Quantum chemistry relies on general-purpose software, whose generality leaves many large-scale calculations beyond practical resource budgets. Coding agents make task-specific programs cheap to write, but not efficient ones easy to find: whether a computational strategy is accurate and fast enough becomes clear only after it actually runs at the target scale. We introduce MakoBORN, a foresighted agentic computing framework that synthesizes high performance quantum chemistry programs on demand. MakoBORN anticipates the behavior of each strategy before execution, extrapolating its error from representative small systems and predicting its runtime from the target-scale workload and measured hardware throughputs. Building on these predictions, MakoBORN unfolds the preset schemes of existing packages into independently configurable algorithmic components, selects the fastest strategy within the error tolerance from the predicted accuracy-runtime Pareto frontier, and guides coding agents to compile it with component-level performance predictions. For a Hartree-Fock calculation with 50,024 basis functions, MakoBORN finishes in 1.41 h on a single CPU node, 77$\times$ faster than the estimated runtime of a general-purpose baseline and still 9.8$\times$ faster with development time included. On a single GPU, MakoBORN completes the ubiquitin calculation in 2.1 h, the same order of runtime as the GPU-accelerated package Mako on 64 GPUs, and shortens the B-DNA duplex calculation from an estimated two months to 8.1 h (173$\times$).

title: FlowBack-Adjoint : Physics-Aware and Energy-Guided Conditional Flow-Matching for Protein Backmapping
abstract: Coarse-grained (CG) molecular models of proteins can substantially increase the time and length scales accessible to molecular dynamics simulations of proteins, but recovery of accurate all-atom (AA) ensembles from CG simulation trajectories can be essential for exposing molecular mechanisms and for the calculation of physical properties requiring atomistic detail. The recently reported deep generative model FlowBack restores AA detail to protein Cα traces using a flow-matching architecture and demonstrates state-of-the-art performance in backmapping of AA structural ensembles (J. Chem. Inf.

title: Impact of culture medium on linezolid PK/PD activity against Staphylococcus aureus in a Hollow-Fiber infection model simulating cerebrospinal fluid exposure
abstract: This study aimed to assess the impact of the culture medium on the effect of linezolid against Staphylococcus aureus using Time-Kill curves (TKC) and Hollow-Fiber infection model (HFIM) by reproducing cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) PK profiles. TKC were performed over 30 h in Mueller-Hinton Broth (MHB), artificial CSF (aCSF) and human CSF (hCSF) at 0, 0.25, 1, 4 x linezolid MIC. Clinical CSF concentrations after 600 or 900 mg q12h and 900 mg q8h were reproduced in HFIM over 96 h in MHB and aCSF. A PK/PD model developed from MHB TKC and HFIM data was combined with hCSF TKC data to predict bacterial counts in HFIM in hCSF. In TKC, bacterial growth was slower in hCSF than MHB. Linezolid was bactericidal in MHB, but only bacteriostatic in hCSF. In aCSF, no growth and no decrease in bacterial counts was observed. In HFIM, bacterial growth was predicted to be also slower in hCSF than MHB. Linezolid at 900 mg q8h was needed to obtain a bactericidal effect in MHB, while 600 mg q12h would be sufficient in hCSF. Despite aCSF renewal in HFIM, no growth and no impact of the treatment was observed whatever linezolid dosing regimen. Bacterial growth and linezolid effect differed between media. MHB overestimated bacterial growth and suggested higher dosing regimen than hCSF, questioning its suitability for central nervous system infections in vitro studies. Using aCSF would be a promising alternative, although its composition requires optimisation to better reproduce bacterial growth and linezolid effect observed in hCSF.

title: Transannular Sigmatropic Rearrangement of Transient Spirocyclic C3 Ammonium Ylides: Stereospecific Access to Bridged Bicyclic Benzo[ b ]azepine Derivatives and Higher Homologues
abstract: We report a stereospecific entry to bicyclic benzo[b]azepines enabled by an unusual sigmatropic [1,5] carbon shift from a transient spirocyclic C3 ammonium enolate. Enantiopure aziridine-substituted chalcones undergo efficient ring expansion to deliver a broad set of benzo[b]azepin-6-ones in consistently high yields with complete transfer of stereochemical information. The strategy is generalized to larger-ring congeners, providing streamlined access to benzo[b]azocines and benzo[b,g]azecines.

title: Contrasting Effects of Potassium Glutamate and Potassium Chloride on the Oligomerization Equilibrium and Kinetics of the PCNA Sliding Clamp
abstract: While salt and osmolyte effects on protein folding have been extensively characterized, their effects on the dissociation equilibria of protein complexes are less well understood. These effects arise from preferential solute interactions with functional groups exposed during unfolding or dissociation, as described quantitatively by the solute partitioning model (SPM). The surface exposed upon unfolding has a remarkably similar functional group composition among globular proteins, leading to broadly similar effects of a given solute on the unfolding free energy. In contrast, the composition of the surface exposed upon dissociation can vary substantially among protein assemblies, making solute effects dependent on the specific interface. Here, we use fluorescence correlation spectroscopy (FCS) to characterize the trimer - monomer equilibrium of the Saccharomyces cerevisiae proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA) sliding clamp in 50-1000mM potassium chloride (KCl) and potassium glutamate (KGlu). KCl, generally a weak stabilizer of folded proteins, had a modest, nonmonotonic effect on PCNA dissociation, with weak stabilization at intermediate concentrations and partial destabilization at higher concentrations. KGlu, a strong stabilizer of folded proteins, progressively stabilized the trimer, decreasing the effective dissociation concentration approximately fivefold between 50 mM and 1000 mM. Kinetic measurements showed that this stabilization arises predominantly from an increase in the association rate constant. Analysis of the crystal structure and molecular dynamics simulations showed that PCNA dissociation exposes a surface enriched in amide oxygen and depleted in hydrocarbon relative to typical unfolding surfaces. Within the SPM, the distinct interactions of KCl and KGlu with these groups provide a molecular rationale for their contrasting effects on PCNA dissociation. These results demonstrate that trends established in protein folding studies cannot be assumed to extend to protein dissociation equilibria.

title: Mechanistic and kinetic insights into secondary phenol formation from cresol and toluene: A combined quantum chemical and machine learning study
abstract: Context In this study, the reaction mechanisms and kinetics of four pathways leading to phenol + CH 3 formation were systematically investigated, including the reactions of o -, m -, and p -cresol with H atoms and the reaction of toluene with OH radicals. The results show that the addition of H atoms to the three cresol isomers requires activation energies of 7.6, 8.4, and 8.6 kcal/mol, respectively, leading to the formation of the corresponding intermediates IS1, IS2, and IS3.

title: Firefly-Geni: Automated Iteration-Guided Generative Discovery of Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence Molecules
abstract: The efficient discovery of thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) molecules remains heavily dependent on expert-driven design rules, while the vast structure–property knowledge accumulated in the literature stays largely fragmented and underutilized. Here, we present Firefly-Geni, an automated and interpretable active-evolution framework that transforms dispersed literature knowledge into structurally novel TADF candidates through a closed-loop workflow. Firefly-Geni integrates large-language-model (LLM)-assisted data extraction, multitask property prediction, conditional molecular generation, and theoretical evaluation. Its data-mining module converts unstructured literature into a curated database of experimental property entries. A dual-molecular-graph multitask predictor and a conditional generator are integrated with quantum-chemical feedback, enabling iterative refinement toward structural novelty. From 100,000 molecules generated under target conditions of a singlet–triplet energy gap ΔEST = 0.05 eV and a synthetic accessibility (SA) score of 2.5, Firefly-Geni identifies 100 structurally novel candidates computationally predicted to support reverse intersystem crossing and to be synthetically tractable, spanning diverse emission wavelengths. One synthesized candidate exhibited an experimental ΔEST of 0.019 eV and a film photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of 84% under nitrogen, broadly consistent with the predicted small gap and high PLQY. Interpretability analyses further reveal chemically meaningful structure–property relationships and generation preferences, confirming that the candidates encode physically relevant low-ΔEST design motifs. This work offers a closed-loop, explainable strategy for actively evolving TADF candidates from literature knowledge, providing a generalizable route for data-driven molecular discovery.

title: Biosynthesis of serotonergic Kanna alkaloids
abstract: Plants have repeatedly evolved to synthesize natural products that exploit serotonin signaling in animals. Although serotonin and most of its neuroactive analogs derive from tryptophan, the medicinal Kanna plant (Mesembryanthemum tortuosum) instead uses tyrosine and phenylalanine to construct a serotonin-like scaffold through unknown chemical transformations. Here, we elucidate the biosynthesis of Kanna alkaloids, including the serotonin reuptake inhibitor mesembrine. We reveal an unusual scaffold-forming strategy that is mediated by non-canonical transferase and oxidase enzymes, and we provide mechanistic insight on how an activated biosynthetic intermediate undergoes a multistep cyclization cascade to form the Kanna alkaloid scaffold. Collectively, our work uncovers how plants repurpose unconventional metabolic building blocks and enzymes to produce serotonergic molecules with promise as therapeutics for neurological disorders.

title: CDK phospho-degron tags for dynamic protein regulation
abstract: Cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) activity underpins cell cycle progression through dynamic and temporally ordered phosphorylation events. While transcriptional regulation has been extensively exploited in synthetic biology, the rational engineering of post-translational signaling circuits remains underdeveloped. Here, we introduce modular CDK-responsive phospho-degron tags derived from the Far1 regulatory region and demonstrate their ability to confer tunable, cell cycle-dependent control over protein stability in budding yeast. By systematically modifying cyclin docking motifs and Cks1 priming sites, we generate degron variants with distinct degradation kinetics and phosphorylation thresholds. These modules enable predictable modulation of transcription factor abundance and downstream gene expression. We further combine CDK-responsive degrons with phosphorylation-controlled localization modules for multi-layered regulation of sequential nuclear import and degradation. We encode multiple kinase activity thresholds within a single protein, demonstrating how complex phosphorylation logic can be compactly implemented. Finally, we show that degron performance is strongly influenced by culture conditions, particularly cell density and associated changes in CDK activity. Together, our results establish CDK-driven phospho-degrons as versatile building blocks for engineering dynamic protein regulation and provide a foundation for constructing synthetic post-translational signaling circuits.

title: Exponent Polytopes for Abstracting Chemical Reaction Networks into Formal Specification Models for Compositional Design of Biomolecular Circuits
abstract: Model based design has shown promise for synthetic biological circuits. However, many approaches remain empirical and limited in scale. Here, we develop specification models from chemical reaction network (CRN) models. These specifications encode assumptions explicitly and guarantees that must be met under those assumptions. Specifically, we show how monomial dominance relations in open CRNs induce polyhedral regime assumptions in logarithmic coordinates. These assumptions give polyhedral assume guarantee contracts that encode system behavior. Further, we show how order of magnitude dominance assumptions can be written explicitly as contract assumptions and used to derive tighter guarantees. We demonstrate two biological circuit design applications: identifying the biological mechanisms that meet the required system-level specification, and screening promoter and ribosome binding site choices to determine expression gains that satisfy a specification through contract composition and refinement. Ultimately, these results provide a path from CRN descriptions of synthetic biological parts to specification-based compositional design.

title: AmberMeta: From AMBER Simulation Files to Checked Protocols and FAIR Metadata
abstract: Molecular dynamics (MD) projects with AMBER often consist of hundreds of runs, and their history is recorded only in the files of these runs. Errors such as a run restarted from the wrong file, a missing or unfinished segment, or a replica that stopped early can therefore pass unnoticed into analyses, Methods sections, and data repositories. Here, we developed AmberMeta, a Python tool that reconstructs the simulation protocol of a finished AMBER project from its files as a draft for the user to review. AmberMeta then checks the reviewed history against the AMBER run outputs and writes a machine-readable record of the runs. This record can serve as findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable (FAIR) metadata of the simulations, for example for databases such as MDDB or for annotation with ontologies such as MOLSIM, and as the factual basis of a Methods section. In 19 in-house projects, some of them still in progress, AmberMeta reported unfinished runs, replicas at different stages of completion, and runs whose files were not collected with them. In copies of eight projects, it reported 146 of 152 deliberately introduced errors. AmberMeta thus helps improve the reliability, reproducibility, and FAIR data management of AMBER simulations by providing a systematic, file-based record of what was actually simulated.

title: UBQLN2, but not an ALS-linked variant, protects client protein from temperature-induced self-association
abstract: Aside from its established role in delivering ubiquitinated substrates for degradation, the proteasomal shuttle factor UBQLN2 also functions as a chaperone, likely via its central STI1 domains. Chaperone activity remains poorly understood due to the lack of known clients. Domesticated retrotransposon protein RTL8 was recently identified as a UBQLN2 interactor, and RTL8's cellular levels are stabilized by UBQLN2. RTL8 is a small protein comprising an N-terminal helix that drives its high-order oligomerization and a C-terminal helical bundle that weakly self-associates, especially at higher temperatures. Here, we provide direct evidence that UBQLN2 acts as a chaperone for RTL8. The N-terminal region of UBQLN2, through its UBL and STI1-I domains, engages RTL8 with low-nanomolar affinity in a sandwich conformation that prevents temperature-dependent self-association of RTL8. Notably, an ALS-linked mutation in the UBQLN2 STI1-I domain reduces RTL8 affinity by an order of magnitude, and impairs the ability of UBQLN2 to protect RTL8 from self-association in vitro and to stabilize RTL8 levels in cells. These findings expand the functional repertoire of UBQLN2 beyond proteasomal shuttling and link its chaperone activity to a disease-relevant mutation.

title: Quantification of Spin Fluctuations during Stem Cell Differentiation Using Diamond Nanopillars
abstract: Quantitative detection of radical-associated magnetic activity in living cells remains challenging because variations between quantum sensors complicate direct comparisons of intracellular environments. Here, we demonstrate a label-free quantum sensing platform based on substrate-fixed diamond nanopillars containing individually addressable nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers. The fixed architecture enables one-to-one measurements using identical NV sensors in the presence and absence of cells, minimizing sensor-to-sensor variability and allowing reliable assessment of cellular contributions to spin decoherence. Cellular compatibility assays supported preserved metabolic activity, DNA synthesis, and membrane integrity without detectable apoptotic activation. Intracellular NV centers retained approximately 10% optically detected magnetic resonance contrast, 20% Rabi contrast, and a Hahn-echo coherence time T2 of approximately 3 {micro}s. Carr-Purcell-Meiboom-Gill dynamical decoupling extended intracellular T2 to 25.8 {+/-} 4.90 {micro}s. We applied this platform to embryonic stem (ES) cells undergoing doxycycline-induced differentiation toward the trophectoderm lineage. Identical NV sensors exhibited consistent coherence recovery following removal of differentiation-induced cells, whereas undifferentiated controls showed no systematic recovery. Calibration using the stable radical TEMPOL, supported by magnetic-noise modeling and kinetic Monte Carlo simulations, enabled numerical evaluation of local magnetic responses as model-dependent TEMPOL-equivalent spin densities of 0.084-0.567 spins/nm3 across different sensing sites. These findings establish a quantitative approach to investigating intracellular physicochemical changes during stem-cell differentiation and demonstrate the potential of quantum sensing to study biological processes relevant to tissue development and regenerative medicine.

title: Cryo-EM structure of plant ABCC1 reveals mode of arsenic transport
abstract: Plant ATP-binding cassette transporter C1 (ABCC1) mediates the vacuolar sequestration of heavy metal-phytochelatin (PC) complexes for cytosolic detoxification, yet the structural mechanisms of substrate recognition and metal coordination remain uncharacterized. Here, we report functional assays and single-particle cryo-EM structures of maize ABCC1 (ZmABCC1) in its apo state and bound to an PC2-As(III) complex. Functional assays demonstrate that ZmABCC1 ATPase activity is sequentially increased by glutathione, PC2, and PC3 in the presence of , supporting that longer PC chain lengths increase transport efficiency. The substrate-bound structure reveals the mode of substrate binding of the heavy metal complex, with the As(III) atom coordinated in a trigonal pyramidal geometry by three sulfur atoms from two PC2 ligands. Arg1200 plays a key role through nonpolar interaction with As(III) through its aliphatic side chain and an electrostatic interaction with the carboxyl group of PC2. These results define the molecular basis of PC-mediated heavy metal transport by plant ABCC1 which could be utilized to inform efforts to engineer crop stress resilience.

title: VISION-GAN: Mask Conditioned U-Net GAN with Multi-Scale Auxiliary Supervision for Retinal Fundus Image Generation
abstract: Retinal fundus imaging is essential for early detection of ocular and systemic disease, but training deep models is limited by data scarcity, privacy constraints, and class imbalance. Existing generative approaches mainly target global realism, with limited control over fine-grained retinal anatomy and lesion patterns. We address this by explicitly conditioning fundus image synthesis on retinal structural and lesion-specific priors.
venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine

title: Protein language model-assisted screening of bitter peptides from Prunus dulcis
abstract: Bitterness is a major limitation in the utilization of plant-derived proteins in food systems, while conventional identification of bitter peptides is labor-intensive and inefficient. Advances in food informatics, particularly protein language models, provide new opportunities for predicting the properties of food chemicals. In this study, we developed a protein language model-assisted workflow to screen and prioritize potential bitter peptides from Prunus dulcis proteins. Protein sequences were first subjected to in silico digestion to generate candidate peptides.

title: Agentic reinforcement learning empowers next-generation chemical language models for molecular design and synthesis
abstract: Language models are revolutionizing the biochemistry domain, assisting scientists in drug design and chemical synthesis with high efficiency. Yet current approaches struggle between small language models prone to hallucination and limited knowledge retention, and large cloud-based language models plagued by privacy risks and high inference costs. To bridge this gap, we introduce ChemCRAFT, a novel framework leveraging agentic reinforcement learning to decouple chemical reasoning from knowledge storage.

title: Rational Design of Molecular Glue Degraders Utilizing Endogenous Transient Protein-Protein Interactions
abstract: Molecular glues are small molecules that modulate protein activity by inducing or stabilizing protein-protein interactions (PPIs). However, identifying and harnessing endogenous protein pairs amenable to small-molecule-mediated stabilization remains a major challenge in molecular glue development. Here we introduce transient interface pocket-guided molecular glue rational design (TrIP-MGRD), a strategy that shifts compound discovery from empirical screening toward rational, interaction-guided design by exploiting druggable pockets at transient PPI interfaces.

title: Antibody full-length light chain reshapes variable domains aggregation without altering their dominance in amyloid fibrils
abstract: AL amyloidosis is a fatal systemic amyloid disease in which antibody light chains (LCs), including full-length (FL) and their proteolytically fragmented variable (VL) and constant (CL) domains, aggregate within a complex extracellular matrix (ECM) across multiple tissues. However, how these co-existing species shape aggregation kinetics, fibril morphology, stability, and toxicity remains unexplored. In this work, using a patient-derived LC (AL55), we show that FL transiently interacts with VL, slowing its aggregation nearly four-fold and diverting it into protease-sensitive, seeding-incompetent protofibrillar aggregates rather than mature amyloid assemblies. VL alone or in the presence of inert CL instead matures into toxic, protease-resistant, seeding-competent helical fibrils. Owing to their greater protease resistance and seeding competence, VL-dominated amyloid assemblies persist and contribute to their enrichment within tissues. The FL-mediated redirection is generic across multiple amyloidogenic VLs. These results reveal that LC aggregation, like that of A{beta} and Tau, is governed by interplay between full-length and fragmented species, rather than VL domain aggregation in isolation. Overall, this work identifies a molecular basis for the selective enrichment of VL fibrils in patients and provides a therapeutic rationale for stabilizing VL domains to prevent their pathological aggregation.

title: A hybrid biophysical-neural network model links nanoscale cardiac junctions to tissue conduction
abstract: Nanoscale structure of the intercalated disk (ID) governs cardiac conduction through gap junctions and ephaptic interactions and is remodeled in arrhythmogenic disease. Computationally expensive models that resolve ID nanostructure have been confined to cables of tens of cells, such that the role of ID nanostructure on conduction has not been testable. Here, we show that a hybrid biophysical-neural network model removes this limit. A memory-based flow map, trained on finite element method (FEM) simulations of single junctions and short cables, defines surrogates that replace each junction in tissue. The hybrid model reproduces action potentials with 1-2 mV RMSE and conduction velocity restitution across multiple ID geometries with a mean error of 0.24%. Without retraining, surrogate models run in 2-D and 3-D tissues, with over one million junctions, 10^4-10^5 times faster than the FEM model and within an order of magnitude of a monodomain model that neglects ID structure. In large tissues with reduced gap-junctional coupling, regional cleft widening blocks conduction, whereas either change alone does not, linking ID remodeling to arrhythmogenic substrate.

title: Continuous Metaheuristic Optimization of Carbon Nanoclusters: Global Minima and Finite-Temperature Thermodynamic Stability
abstract: Accurate structure prediction requires thorough energy landscape exploration, yet exhaustive search remains computationally intractable. While diverse strategies ranging from basin hopping to genetic algorithms have been implemented to map these landscapes, particle swarm optimization (PSO) has proven to be a particularly powerful approach for high-dimensional search.

title: High-Throughput Workflow for Polaron-Resolved Modeling of Reduced Ceria
abstract: Understanding the reduction of cerium oxide is key to optimize its performance in catalytic and technological applications. However, resolving the complex interplay between oxygen vacancies and Ce3+ polarons at high reduction levels is challenging because the vast configurational space of vacancy defects and polaron distributions grows exponentially with the degree of CeO2 reduction. Foundation machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) cannot resolve polaronic configurations in reduced ceria, making spin-polarized density functional theory with Hubbard corrections (DFT+U) essential.

title: Soluble Electrocatalytic Cobalt Redox Polymer for the Electrochemical Reduction of CO2
abstract: Extending molecular electrocatalysts into multimetallic catalyst architectures is a promising strategy for converting waste CO2 into value-added chemicals in the electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR). We have prepared a soluble multimetallic polymeric catalyst, poly- [Co(VinylPDI)], through the radical polymerization of vinyl group attached to a Co(pyridyldiimine) building unit.

title: Protein chemical shift prediction in web browsers: seven major programs ported, benchmarked, and studied for what they help to reveal about NMR structures, AlphaFold models and molecular simulations
abstract: Motivation. Predicting NMR chemical shifts from protein structures is routine in structure validation, resonance assignment and the analysis of molecular dynamics simulations, but the available programs come as platform-specific executables, aging software stacks or upload-based servers, and some are no longer distributed. Results. Assisted by Claude Code, I ported seven chemical shift predictors to run entirely in the web browser with no installation and no data leaving the user's computer: UCBShift-X, SHIFTX2, SPARTA+, PPM_One (with its MD-ensemble variant PPM), CamShift, LEGOLAS and the…

title: CHELATE: High-precision structure prediction for metalloproteins
abstract: Accurate prediction of ligand binding modes in non-heme metalloproteins remains challenging because conventional docking methods often fail to correctly identify poses with accurate metal-coordination geometries. Here, we introduce CHELATE, a machine learning-based post-docking filter that predicts the root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) of ligand metal-binding groups (MBGs) to filter out inaccurate poses and prioritise those with native-like metal coordination.

title: Full-Factorial Formulation Screening and Model Protein Sensing with Electropolymerized Molecularly Imprinted Polymer-Modified Electrodes
abstract: Studies of electropolymerized molecularly imprinted polymers (e-MIPs) for macromolecular targets typically adopt formulations from prior systems or optimize them one factor at a time (OFAT), leaving component-level interactions uncharacterized. Using a full-factorial design, we screened 36 e-MIP formulations on gold screen-printed electrodes (e-MIP/SPEs), varying crosslinker concentration (C C ), monomer-to-crosslinker molar ratio (M:C), and template concentration (C T ).

title: Metastable Olivine-Type Intermediates in Maricite NaFePO4 Cycling Revealed by Operando XRD and DFT
abstract: NaFePO4 (NFP) is a potential cathode material for sodium-ion batteries and exists mainly as the maricite and olivine polymorphs. Maricite NaFePO4 (m-NFP) is the thermodynamically stable and synthetically accessible polymorph of NaFePO4, with a theoretical capacity of 154 mAh g-1 but is expected to exhibit limited electrochemical activity due to the absence of continuous Na-ion migration channels in its crystal structure.

title: A Revised Force Field Parameterization for Iodine-Based Halogen-Bonded Cocrystals
abstract: Halogen-bonded cocrystals have garnered attention due to their structural diversity and functional applications. Prediction of their crystal structures opens wide opportunities for computationally-driven design of functional materials based on halogen bonding. Crucial prerequisite for reliable crystal structure prediction (CSP) of halogen-bonded materials is a fast yet accurate method of relative energy ranking of the predicted structures.

title: Predicting Solvent-Induced Changes in Fluorescence Quantum Yield: Direct ClassificationVersus Regression
abstract: Changing the solvent can alter a molecule’s fluorescence quantum yield. This study compares two structure-based methods for predicting such changes: direct classification and prediction of two quantum yields followed by subtraction. From FluoDB-Lite, we retained 12,157 measurements for 2,712 molecules, resulting in 29,550 within-paper solvent comparisons. We categorized changes as reduced, approximately unchanged, or enhanced using a provisional absolute tolerance of 0.10. Molecules were divided into training, validation, and test sets without identity overlap.

title: The rise of AI in mathematics — and science
abstract: We discuss the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in mathematical research and explore its implications for the computational science community.

title: Repurposed battery molecules drive key chemical reactions where oil meets water
abstract: The process of producing essential medicines and fine chemicals has long been powered by reactions involving intense heat, heavy-metal catalysts and hazardous hydrogen gas. Now, a team of Harvard chemists and engineers has demonstrated that these critical transformations can be driven cleanly by electricity, right at the boundary where oil and water meet.

title: Molecular Controls of Doping-Induced Chain Stiffness in Conjugated Polymers
abstract: Electronic doping planarizes conjugated polymer backbones and enhances quinoidal character, but its effects on chain-scale conformations relevant to packing, orientation, and charge transport remain poorly understood. Predicting these effects is challenging because electronic delocalization and backbone rotation are nonlocally coupled. Here, we develop a coarse-grained tight-binding molecular dynamics model that incorporates nonlocal electronic contributions to backbone rotational forces to predict dopingdependent conjugation and persistence lengths.

title: Chemically specific NMR relaxation in thermally modified mesoporous materials
abstract: Low-field nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) relaxation provides a non-invasive method for characterising solid–liquid interactions within porous materials. However, the influence of pore surface chemistry on the surface relaxivity of different liquid adsorbates remains poorly understood. In this study, we investigate the effects of thermal surface modification on eight liquid adsorbates (cyclohexane, acetone and six alcohols) confined within mesoporous silicas and γ-alumina using low-field (12.7 MHz) two-dimensional 1 H T 1 – T 2 relaxation measurements.

title: Heterostructured BiVO4/g-C3N4 Semiconductor Nanomaterials for Enhanced Visible-Light-Driven Degradation and Mineralization of Emerging Water Contaminants
abstract: The persistence of emerging contaminants (ECs)—including pharmaceuticals, endocrine-disrupting compounds, and synthetic dyes—in aquatic ecosystems poses a critical threat to environmental and public health due to their resistance to conventional wastewater treatment processes. Semiconductor photocatalysis offers a sustainable, solar-driven pathway for complete pollutant mineralization, yet single-component photocatalysts suffer from rapid electron–hole recombination and limited visible-light utilization.

title: Double-hybrid quality reactivity in converged quantum environments at GGA-like speed: comparing local correlation and local quantum embedding accelerations
abstract: Double-hybrid (DH) density functionals provide the highest rung of DFT accuracy, but their MP2-like term can be computationally prohibitive, when including realistic chemical environments. Here, we extend our local embedded subsystem (LESS) framework, previously introduced for projector- and Huzinaga-equation-based quantum embedding for hybrid DFT-in-GGA, by implementing DH-in-DFT embedding with hybrid or GGA DFT environments.

title: Deuteration as a General Strategy to Enhance Small Molecule-Based Photodynamic Therapy
abstract: Utilizing isotope effects has a long history in organic chemistry, and has recently been shown to improve fluorophore photophysics and azobenzene-based photoswitch kinetics. Herein, we report the deuteration of methylene blue (MB) and sulfonated tetraphenyl porphyrin (TPPS), both far-red singlet oxygen sensitizers (SOSs), which boosts the efficiency of reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation by >55%.

title: Functionalized 2-Substituted Oxetanes through Epoxide Ring Expansion
abstract: The value of an oxetane building block depends on access to both its substitution pattern and a functional group that can be modified without consuming the ring. We examined the Corey-Chaykovsky ring expansion of alcohol-derived epoxides as an entry to functionalized 2-substituted oxetanes. Benzyl-protected allylic alcohols provided precursors for varying side-chain branching and substitution at the future C2 center.

title: A Frontside S N 2 Glycosylation Reaction
abstract: Understanding and controlling the stereochemical outcome of glycosylation reactions remains a fundamental challenge in synthetic carbohydrate chemistry. The S N 1-S N 2 reaction mechanism continuum is commonly employed to account for the stereochemistry of glycosylation reactions and to explain the reactivity of reactive intermediates. In this continuum, covalent anomeric triflates serve as glycosylating species in backside S N 2 (S N 2- b ) pathways, and triflate ion – oxocarbenium ion pairs are central on the S N 1-side of the spectrum.
authors: Koen N. A. van de Vrande

title: Mechanism in Structure: Narrated and Interactive Tutorials on Hemoglobin and Chymotrypsin Built from Protein Data Bank Structures
abstract: Students usually meet an enzyme mechanism as a two-dimensional textbook figure and the enzyme itself as a separate threedimensional image, and the two rarely meet. This article describes two tutorials that place each mechanistic step in the real structure, beside a two-dimensional panel drawn after the course textbook. The hemoglobin tutorial follows the T→R transition: the iron moving into the heme plane, the rotation of one αβ dimer against the other, the ion pairs that break, the central cavity and the Bohr effect.

title: Spatial arrangement of bonds governs the thermodynamics of multivalent DNA origami interfaces
abstract: Multivalency, the simultaneous engagement of many weak bonds, underlies recognition between cells, viruses, and proteins and enables assembly of DNA origami into micrometer-scale structures. Predicting the stability of a multivalent interface is difficult because each bond's contribution depends on the number, strength, and arrangement of the other bonds and on the scaffold that presents them, which rarely vary independently.

title: Electronic versus magnetic descriptors of excited-state (anti)aromaticity: a critical assessment for singlet and triplet states
abstract: Excited-state aromaticity (ESA) and antiaromaticity (ESAA) are important concepts for understanding photochemical and photophysical processes. To quantify their extent and to follow ESA gain and ESAA relief, it would be beneficial to have aromaticity indices that are readily computable for higher excited states, applicable independently of the spin multiplicity, and suitable for non-equilibrium geometries. However, current aromaticity indices remain difficult to evaluate beyond the lowest triplet state and away from equilibrium structures.

title: Phosphorus-Functionalized Carbon Quantum Dot-Doped Alginate Beads for Rapid and High-Capacity Recovery of Rare Earth Elements
abstract: Recovering rare earth elements (REEs) from waste streams requires adsorbents that combine rapid uptake, high capacity, and effective regeneration. Here, phosphorus-functionalized carbon quantum dots immobilized on alginate beads (P-CQD/ALG) were developed to integrate REE-binding functionality with a readily separable solid form. First, phosphorus functionalization (P-CQD/ALG) showed substantially higher Ce3+ removal than pristine alginate and unmodified or nitrogen-functionalized CQD composites, suggesting P-CQD/ALG as an optimal adsorbent.

title: Divergent Synthesis of Diazaspiroalkanes through Spirolactam Intermediates
abstract: The use of spirocyclic diamines in molecular design requires both access to the desired framework and control over the nitrogen available for functionalization. We describe a divergent synthesis that addresses these requirements through common spirolactam intermediates. Starting from three commercially available methyl N-Boc cyclic amino esters, cyanoalkylation and nitrile reduction/lactamization afforded six frameworks. Two complementary benzyl/Boc sequences then delivered 11 mono-Boc diamines in final preparations of 1.8-25 g, including five pairs with opposite protection arrangements.

title: Kinetic-thermodynamic symmetry breaking in reversible two-step polycondensation
abstract: Reversible step-growth polycondensation underpins the industrial manufacture of polyamides, polyesters and polycarbonates. Yet its classical Carothers–Flory description, built on Flory’s principle of equal reactivity and on a closed-system treatment, leaves a family of recurring process anomalies outside any single theoretical framework. Here we extend the asymmetric two-step pairing scheme of the companion theory with a reverse selectivity β and introduce an independent activity factor χ for the by-product (water), obtaining a closed-form, three-parameter theory of the equilibrium structure…

title: Site-Selective Peripheral Aryl Substitution Tunes Red-to-Near-Infrared Fluorescence in Thienopyrazine-Fused Pyrene Heteroacenes
abstract: We report four thienopyrazine-fused pyrene heteroacenes with aryl substituents varied at the pyrene core and flanking thiophene rings. Compounds 1–3 exhibit neat-film photoluminescence quantum yields of 64–88% at 564–589 nm, whereas compound 4 displays an emission maximum at 767 nm in solution. Single-crystal analysis of 2 shows that cofacial p–p interactions between the central aromatic cores are impeded. The results show that both the position and identity of peripheral aryl substituents influence the photoluminescence properties of a common heteroacene framework.

title: Minimalist catalyst for excellent tacticity: Stereocontrolled radical polymerization with Lewis acids
abstract: Stereoregular vinyl polymers are made by coordination or anionic polymerization, whereas radical polymerization, the dominant industrial route, offers little stereocontrol. We report a simple Lewis acid–mediated reversible addition–fragmentation chaintransfer polymerization: with only 3.3 mol% samarium Lewis acid, polymerization of more than a dozen functionalized acrylamides reaches up to 97% m diad selectivity, the highest tacticity in homogeneous radical polymerization of a commodity monomer.

title: Marine Exopolysaccharide Diabolican Enhances the Physical Properties of Collagen Hydrogels via a Temperature-Dependent Polyionic Complexation
abstract: Collagens and glycosaminoglycans are essential components of the extracellular matrix, providing key biochemical and mechanical properties. Type I collagen and hyaluronan (HA) are therefore widely used in tissue engineering to mimic the characteristics of human tissues. However, native HA does not significantly improve the properties of collagen hydrogels when combined with this biopolymer. In this study, the marine exopolysaccharide diabolican (HE800 strain), which exhibits structural similarities to HA, was evaluated as an alternative glycosaminoglycan for combination with type I collagen.

title: A shared formulation design space reveals poly(2-ethyl-2oxazoline) chain length as a determinant of lipid nanoparticle performance and relative organ distribution
abstract: The interface between lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) and their biological environment represents a key determinant of biodistribution. Here, we investigated poly(2-ethyl-2oxazoline) (PEtOx)-lipids as an adaptable component of this interface and determined how polymer chain length affects LNP formulation as well as biological behavior. Rather than comparing different polymers with a single nominal formulation composition, we first mapped the pharmaceutical design space of four PEtOx-lipids containing average chain lengths of 20, 34, 49, or 71 repeating units and identified formulation conditions…

title: Stability and Raman Spectra of Carbon Nanotube Fragments across Chirality and Length
abstract: Bare-ended carbon nanotube (CNT) fragments restructure at their rims. Geometry screening and density functional vibrational analysis identify 13 local minima on the restricted-singlet surface; six have stable restricted solutions. Energy per carbon, fitted to the inverse squared mean optimized diameter and separate initial armchair-like and zigzag-like rim fractions (R2 = 0.993), gives effective end coefficients of 2.12 and 2.64 eV per initial rim carbon, respectively. Eleven minima contain 58 short end pairs and 58 high-frequency, mainly collective pair-stretching modes.

title: Frustrated Lewis Pairs upon UV light absorption: ground vs excited state mechanisms in CO2 adduct formation.
abstract: The broadly reported increase in atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) concentration is a major contributor to global climate change. In response, substantial efforts are being directed toward the development of low-carbon energy systems and the identification of efficient CO₂ capture technologies to mitigate the excessive greenhouse gas emissions. Among these, solid sorbent-based capture methods have attracted significant attention.[1] However, a key limitation of such approaches lies in the regeneration of the sorbent material, which often requires energy-intensive processes.[1,2] To address…

title: The photoelectric effect as frequency coupling: a spectral law without work function, photons, electrons or energy
Donor and Acceptor Branching Suppresses Hydrogen-Bond Cooperativity in Mixed (NH3)m(H2S)n Clusters
abstract: Ammonia and hydrogen sulfide are both weak hydrogen-bond (HB) donors, yet each molecule can donate and accept more than one HB, so their mixed networks branch readily. We use the molecular tailoring approach (MTA) at the MP2/aug-cc-pVTZ level to obtain the energy of every HB in 20 neutral (NH3)m(H2S)n clusters (m+ n = 3–7) and to split each energy into an isolated-dimer term and a cooperative term.

title: Enabling rational design in flow organolithium chemistry through data-driven guidelines for substrate selection, reaction choice, and electrophile compatibility
abstract: A practical setup for continuous-flow organolithium chemistry is presented, based on >1000 substrate-electrophile combinations across aromatic, heteroaromatic, and aliphatic scaffolds, including “enabling” building blocks. Despite flow lithiation's recognized advantages in heat transfer and reproducibility, systematic criteria for predicting which transformations translate well to continuous operation, and which should remain batch, have been lacking.

title: Grain Boundary and Stress Evolution during Thin Film Growth: Key Factors Governing the Resistive Hydrogen-Sensing Characteristics of Palladium Thin Films
abstract: Palladium thin film resistive hydrogen sensors have attracted considerable attention due to their high selectivity and low-temperature operation, yet the microstructural mechanisms governing their sensing performance remain insufficiently understood. Here, we establish a processingstructure-property framework by integrating controlled Pd film growth, sensing-performance evaluation, multiscale structural characterization, electron-transport modeling, and DFT calculations.

title: Synthesis and Reactivity of Spirocyclopropyl Amines: A New Class of Conformationally Constrained Building Blocks for Drug Discovery
abstract: Spirocyclopropyl amines combine the conformational constraint of a spiro center with the electronic character of the cyclopropane ring, yet saturated azaspirocycles bearing two such rings remain scarce. Herein, we report the synthesis of mono- and dispiro-cyclopropyl saturated N-heterocycles from readily available lactams and cyclic imides via the Kulinkovich-de Meijere reaction and its Bertus-Szymoniak modification.

title: A stopping rule for completing computed phase diagrams with generative models
abstract: Phase diagrams constructed using known phases misjudge stability when key phases are missing. Generative models supply as many structures as needed, but how many structures to generate and which diagrams will change are unknown. We add 10,000 MatterGen structures per system, relaxed with a machine learning interatomic potential, to Materials Project (MP) data for six Li–transition-metal–O ternaries and track the hull convergence.

title: Biorelevant Triplet μ1,2-Peroxodicopper(II) Intermediates in a Bis(tridentate) Dinucleating Ligand Framework
abstract: Type III dicopper proteins function as O2 carriers and catalysts for hydroxylation reactions, and our understanding of relevant Cu2/O2 intermediates has benefited greatly from studying synthetic analogues. The O2 binding mode in synthetic peroxo intermediates is strongly dependent on ligand effects, including the denticity of the ligand. Here we report a first example of a μ1,2-peroxodicopper(II) complex with bioinspired {N3} coordination that emulates the proposed initial stages of O2 binding in dicopper proteins.

title: Fragility and optionality in process systems engineering
abstract: Process systems engineering (PSE) is broadly about developing methods to guide chemical engineering decisions on the synthesis and analysis of process systems. This definition of Takamatsu (1983) still holds for our field, and so does the problem he left open for us, namely how to synthesise a process system inside a larger system, the world around it, which sets its inputs, outputs and objectives and which it can neither control nor know in advance. Every large process system is unique. It is built once, at one place and time, and it lives only one future.

title: Boronium-Based Ionic Liquids: From an Unusual Main-Group Cation to Functional Ionic Materials
abstract: Boronium-based ionic liquids, sometimes referred to by the acronym “BILs”—are salts in which the cation is a tetra-coordinate, boron-centred molecular ion, and which occupy a distinctive intersection of main-group, coordination and ionic liquid chemistry. Their modern development largely began with robust L1L2BH2+ ions (L = Lewis-base ligand) and the recognition that appropriate ligand and anion choices can render these salts room-temperature liquids.

title: A Rigid Diene, Two Electron Counts: 16– and 18–Electron Ni(0) Olefin Complexes
abstract: We report the application of a rigid polycyclic cage–diene (PCCD) as a ligand for Ni(0) complexation. Microcrystal electron diffraction (MicroED) of Ni(PCCD)2 revealed a mixture of isomers: 16-electron Ni(η4–PCCD)(η2–PCCD) and 18-electron Ni(η4–PCCD)2 complexes. Compared to commercially available Ni(0) sources, Ni(PCCD)2 exhibited comparable catalytic activity in Buchwald–Hartwig aminations.

title: Ligand-Coupled Electron Transfer Enables Highly Stable Two-Electron Electrochemical Energy Storage using a Nickel Bis(diphosphine) Complex
abstract: Here, we show that highly stable two-electron (2e−) energy storage is achieved using [NiII(dppe)2](BF4)2 (dppe = 1,2-bis(diphenylphosphino)ethane) in combination with chloride and bromide salts and excess dppe ligand. Halide coordination to [NiII(dppe)2] 2+ is shown to yield mono-halide [NiII(dppe)2X]+ and bis-halide NiII(dppe)X2 complexes in equilibrium (KCl = 1.4 and KBr = 0.015), both of which are reduced by 2e− to yield Ni0(dppe)2.

title: Scalable Alkylation-Cyclization Strategy for Bridgehead-Functionalized Fused Tetrahydrofurans
abstract: This study presents a practical and scalable synthetic platform for the preparation of functionalized fused tetrahydrofuran building blocks, addressing a current gap in the accessible chemical space. The methodology is based on an alkylation/cyclization sequence of readily available cyclic β-ketoesters with 1,2-dibromoethane under mild K2CO3/18-crown-6 conditions. The transformation proceeds in a single operational step, avoids hazardous reagents, and was demonstrated on a multigram scale.

title: Site-Selected Oxygen K-Edge X-ray Circular Dichroism in Methyl Lactate−Water: Electronic-State Character, Intermolecular Proximity, and Spectral Cancellation
abstract: Hydrogen bonding can place an achiral molecular fragment in a chiral environment, yet the electronic character and methodological robustness of its site-selected X-ray circular-dichroism response remain challenging to establish. Here, we investigate oxygen K-edge excitations in a hydrogen-bonded methyl (S)-lactate−water complex using r 2 SCAN-3c geometries, siterestricted TDA-TDDFT, and natural transition orbital (NTO) analysis.

title: GPU-Accelerated Evaluation of MP2 Correlation Energy Densities for Machine Learning of Density Functionals
abstract: Second-order Møller–Plesset (MP2) correlation energy densities can serve as ingredients for machine learning (ML) of density functionals that improve upon MP2-based double hybrids. However, limitations of existing implementations have restricted the evaluation of these energy densities and of ML-based functionals employing them to small systems. Here, we develop a GPU-accelerated implementation for evaluating MP2 correlation energy densities and their regularized and spin-resolved variants by combining a density fitting scheme that preserves high pointwise accuracy with memory-efficient…

title: Cross-Scale Structural Evolution in 2D Silicon Nanosheet Anodes upon Electrochemical Cycling
abstract: Silicon is a high-capacity anode material for lithium-ion batteries, but the large volume change accompanying lithiation drives structural degradation across multiple length scales. Reducing silicon to a two-dimensional architecture has been explored as a strategy to accommodate lithiation-induced deformation yet whether morphological stability of individual silicon nanosheets translates into dimensional stability of the composite electrode remains unclear.

title: Impact of 2,2’-Substitution on the Pi-Conjugation and Electronic and Optical Properties of Biphenyl-Based Molecules
abstract: Developing strategies to tune excitons or generate Wannier excitons in organic small molecules (OSMs) is an important area of research for advancing photoinduced processes in these materials. Density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) calculations were carried out to investigate intermonomer conjugation in six functionalized benzene monomers and their corresponding six functionalized bisphenol dimers. The study considered two electron-donating substituents (–NH2 and –OCH3) and four electron-withdrawing substituents (–Cl, –Br, –CN, and –NO2).

title: Light-Driven Active Transport across a Liquid Membrane via Photoswitch Sensitization
abstract: Active transport across membranes is essential in living systems, but its implementation in artificial systems remains challenging. Light-driven active transport based on photoswitchable carriers requires differential illumination on the opposite sides of the membrane, a constraint that prevents its application to nanoscale membranes. Here, we introduce a photosensitization-based strategy that enables active transport across a liquid membrane using a single light source.

title: Forced Degradation of Bromantane: Preliminary Characterization of an Oxidative Degradation Product Using Liquid Chromatography and High-Resolution Mass Spectrometry
abstract: Bromantane (N-(4-bromophenyl)adamantan-2-amine) is a synthetic adamantane derivative developed as an antiasthenic pharmaceutical agent in Russia. Despite its pharmaceutical applications and relevance to anti-doping analysis, the chemical degradation pathways of bromantane remain insufficiently characterized. This study investigated the forced-degradation behavior of bromantane under acidic, alkaline, thermal, and oxidative conditions using liquid chromatography with ultraviolet detection (LC-UV) and Orbitrap high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS).

title: A Computational Protocol for Accurate Pressure-Dependent Rates in Barrierless Addition Reactions: CN and C 2 H Reactivity with Ethylene
abstract: The accurate determination of rate coefficients and product branching fractions for multi-well reactions with barrierless entrance and/or exit channels remains a major challenge in computational kinetics, particularly when widely different temperature and pressure regimes must be considered. Here, we introduce a general computational protocol for the case of addition reactions that integrates accurate yet affordable electronic-structure calculations with statistical kinetic treatments tailored to the different elementary reaction steps and a multi-well master-equation approach.

title: Optical Polymer Structure Recognition with PolymerScribe and an Iterative Train-Predict-Correct Workflow
abstract: Immensely valuable polymer information remains functionally inaccessible, trapped in the chemical structure images of legacy and contemporary publications. However, without labels such as molblocks or string representations, those images are not directly processible by cheminformatic tools for downstream applications. This work develops an image recognition model, PolymerScribe, and demonstrates an iterative train-predict-correct workflow for curating labeled polymer structures from the literature.

title: PanJAK: predicting selectivity across the JAK family with deep learning
abstract: Predicting selectivity between closely related protein targets remains a major challenge in drug discovery. While drug-target affinity (DTA) models typically focus on predicting activity against individual targets, selectivity depends on resolving differences in activity between them. Here, we introduce panJAK, a DTA framework to predict selectivity across the four Janus kinase (JAK) paralogs.

title: Stable Pt Single Atoms Embedded in Ge(001) Enable Efficient Hydrogen Evolution
abstract: Single-atom catalysts offer a promising route to maximize noble-metal utilization, but maintaining isolated active sites under operating conditions remains a major challenge. Pt deposition on Ge(001) induces the spontaneous formation of thermodynamically stable nanowire arrays in which Pt atoms remain atomically dispersed within the Ge lattice, creating well-defined single-atom catalytic sites.

title: Multidisciplinary Design and Characterization of Novel cis- and trans-Ferrocene–Platinum Anticancer Candidates
abstract: The limitations of the classical platinum-based drugs (i.e. cisplatin, carboplatin, oxaliplatin), such as adverse side-effects and drug resistance, highlight the need to develop alternative metal-based anticancer compounds. In this context, molecules that bear two pharmacologically active motifs represent a versatile strategy, as they may enhance therapeutic efficacy through synergistic effects, being the synthesis of this type of drugs a promising research field.

title: Beyond Storage Modulus: Toward Application-Relevant Rheological Assessment of Dynamic Hydrogels
abstract: Hydrogels designed for injection and extrusion-based bioprinting experience a sequence of mechanical environments that a single small-amplitude storage-modulus value cannot capture. Before processing, a formulation may need to remain homogeneous and resist premature flow; during delivery, it must deform under device-imposed stresses without excessive pressure or payload damage; after deposition, it must recover sufficiently to retain its intended geometry; and during subsequent use, it must respond appropriately to sustained loading, fluid exchange, degradation, and cell-generated forces.

title: Predicting nanosurface properties via Rayleigh instability
abstract: The surface tension, γ , of nanoscale clusters deviates from its planar limit, γ∞, based on the value of the Tolman length, δ , which is difficult to compute. In this study, we introduce a new method that exploits the Rayleigh instability of charged nanosurfaces to compute both γ∞ and δ properties. By combining Tolman’s γ formulation with the Rayleigh limit we compute these properties only based on the cluster size and charge under which the instability is triggered.

title: Microstructure-resolved modeling of fused filament fabrication of lithium-ion battery electrodes
abstract: Lithium-ion battery (LIB) electrode microstructure can be flexibly tailored via solvent-free extrusion followed by fused filament fabrication (FFF) printing. However, the influence of extrusion and printing process parameters on the final electrode microstructure, properties, and electrochemical performance remains insufficiently explored and has never been investigated through computational modeling. Herein, we introduce a sequential, particle-resolved framework that transfers heterogeneous filaments from our previously developed twin-screw extrusion model into FFF simulations.

title: Radical Sorting Enables Semiconductor-Driven Redox-Neutral C(sp 3 )–C(sp 3 ) Cross-Coupling
abstract: Selective formation of C(sp3)–C(sp3) bonds from carbon-centered radicals is inherently challenging, because competing radical homocoupling can compromise product selectivity. Here, we combine heterogeneous semiconductor photocatalysis with nickel-mediated radical sorting to achieve redox-neutral C(sp3)–C(sp3) bond formation. Under irradiation, graphitic carbon nitride (gCN) generates alkyl radicals from carboxylic acids and redox-active esters (RAEs) through complementary oxidative and reductive single-electron transfer, respectively, without the need for stoichiometric oxidants or…

title: Apparent Recovery Reverses Healing-Rate Rankings Among Soft Polymers
abstract: Abstract Autonomous self-healing at room temperature can extend polymer lifetimes, but combining rapid healing with mechanical robustness remains challenging. Tensile toughness recovery is widely used to compare polymers and infer healing mechanisms. However, the chain mobility enabling healing also permits large bulk deformation and stress redistribution during testing, masking residual interfacial weakness.

title: The Nature of Protein Hierarchies and Implications for Hierarchical Modelling: An AI-Assisted Computational Study with Statistical Mechanics, Information Theory and Unsupervised Learning
abstract: Proteins are widely described as hierarchies of nested structural units, and hierarchical models are widely used to simulate them, yet what kind of hierarchy proteins actually possess, and what that hierarchy implies for how they should be modelled, has not been established. This work addresses these two questions directly. It builds on three earlier studies from this laboratory, on foldability of lattice proteins, on the relationship between folding and function, and on elastic network models (GNM and ANM) of real proteins, which established hierarchical modularity but left its physical…

title: Engineering Stable and Targeted NIR/SWIR Imaging Agents through Metal-Organic Framework Nanoconfinement
abstract: Near-infrared (NIR) and shortwave infrared (SWIR) fluorophores offer significant potential for biomedical imaging owing to their deep tissue penetration and low background autofluorescence. However, their widespread application remains limited by poor aqueous solubility, aggregation-induced fluorescence loss, and inadequate stability in physiological environments.

title: Thermodynamic Model of Mixing and Photo-Demixing in MAPb(I,Br)3 from Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics
abstract: Mixed-halide lead perovskites are promising materials for solar cells because of high photoconversion efficiencies and bandgaps that can be finely tuned through composition, but their application is limited by reversible light-induced halide segregation. Here, we investigate the thermodynamic origin of the segregation behaviour in MAPb(I,Br)3 by combining molecular dynamics, based on a machine-learned interatomic potential fine-tuned to r2SCAN density-functional-theory data, with a model for the electronic and elastic contributions that arise under illumination.

title: How Composition and Cluster Structure Influence CO Adsorption in Pt and Pt–Ge Clusters
abstract: Ge incorporation can weaken CO adsorption on Pt clusters, but it also changes their geometry and bonding. We combine density functional theory with advanced chemical bonding analysis to examine the interplay between composition, geometry, electronic structure, and CO adsorption in ten-atom Pt10, Pt6Ge4, Pt5Ge5, and Pt4Ge6 clusters. By generating derivative structures through Pt/Ge substitution in previously reported global-minimum geometries, we examine how composition and starting structure affect CO binding.

title: Solvent-Directed Heat Shock for Engineering Emissive States in Nonconjugated Polymers: Towards Single-Component Cool-White Light Emission
abstract: Non-conjugated polymers can be engineered into highly photoluminescent materials without conventional πconjugated chromophores by activating their through-space electronic states. However, the development of a low-energy cluster-state emitter from a simple polymer without chemical modification remains a fundamental challenge. We report here a solvent-directed heat-shock approach that reconfigures the excited-state landscape of the water-soluble, biocompatible, carbonyl-rich pharmaceutical binder polymer poly(vinylpyrrolidone) (weak high-energy emitter).

title: Copper-Mediated Bromodeboronation of Alkenyl Pinacol Boronates: Scope and Stereochemical Outcome
abstract: A practical approach to functionalized alkenyl bromides based on CuBr 2 -mediated bromodeboronation of alkenyl pinacol boronates was developed. The target products were obtained in THF/H2O (10:1) at 70 °C in 35–90% yield from acyclic as well as four- to seven-membered carbocyclic and heterocyclic precursors. The reaction was compatible with N -Boc-protected amines, ethers, sulfones, fluorinated groups, esters, and a free carboxylic acid and could be performed on a multigram scale. Flexible boronates bearing pendant nucleophilic groups and an allylic bromide were not tolerated.

title: ORGANOSILICA NANOPARTICLE FORMATION FROM AROMATIC SILANES
abstract: The synthesis and morphological evolution of aromatic organosilica nanoparticles were investigated to elucidate the in luence of intermolecular 𝜋𝜋-𝜋𝜋 interactions and precursor hydrolysis-condensation kinetics. A series of silane precursors comprising monoaryl (PTMS, PTES, PETMS), diaryl (DPDMS, DPDES), functionalized aromatic (CMPETMS), and non-aromatic cyclohexyl (CHTMS) analogs were evaluated across acidic, neutral, and basic reaction environments.

title: Electrifying nonaqueous hydrogenation via aqueous redox and Pickering particle mediation
abstract: Electrocatalytic hydrogenation uses electricity and water to reduce organic compounds, potentially producing high-value chemicals with adjustable selectivity and reaction rate. However, many organic reactants have low solubility in water, limiting the utility of aqueous electroreduction. Meanwhile, nonaqueous electroreduction is likewise limited by the low ionic conductivity of these compounds and the difficulty of product separation.

title: Multigram Synthesis of Enantioenriched α-Aminoboronates and Their α-Quaternary Analogs by Copper-Catalyzed Borylation of Ellman’s N-Sulfinyl Imines
abstract: A practical copper-catalyzed borylation of N - tert -butanesulfinyl aldimines was developed, using CuCl, PCy 3 ·HBF 4 , NaO t Bu, and MeOH as the proton source. Both enantiomers of α-aminoboronate hydrochlorides were obtained via a two-step protocol (borylation – desulfinylation) in 48–66% yield and with 92–98% ee starting from ( R )- or ( S )- tert -butanesulfinamide; the products were isolated by simple filtration from the crude reaction mixture.

title: Pharmaceutical wastewater remediation: occurrence, risk assessment, biological and advanced treatment technologies, and regulatory drivers
abstract: Pharmaceutically active compounds (PhACs) reach surface waters through municipal sewage, hospital effluent, and discharges from drug manufacturing, and conventional treatment removes many of them only partially. In this review, we bring together measured occurrence, risk, and performance data to compare conventional, biological, bioremediation, and advanced physicochemical options.

title: Process Simulation and Techno-Economic Analysis of a Carbon-Negative Rice Husk Biorefinery
abstract: Rice husk, an abundant Indian agricultural waste, represents a critical feedstock for carbon-negative fuel production. This study presents a process simulation and techno-economic analysis (TEA) of a 2G biorefinery integrating bioenergy with carbon capture and storage (BECCS). Modeled in DWSIM, the facility processes 84,000 tonnes/year of rice husk to produce 29.87 million liters of bioethanol via enzymatic hydrolysis and fermentation (75.4% theoretical yield). Energy deficits are offset by a co-located 4.7 MW solar PV installation.

title: Development of Covalent Cyclic Peptide Ligands for the NUP98::KDM5A Oncofusion through Sulfur(VI) Fluoride Reactivity Tuning
abstract: Covalent labeling of nucleophilic amino acids is a useful strategy for liganding ‘difficult-to-drug’ protein targets. Targeting cysteine has been highly successful because of its high nucleophilicity. Covalent ligands that modify lysine residues can provide broader proteome coverage for covalent inhibition. Sulfur(VI) fluorides are lysine-reactive electrophiles with highly tunable intrinsic reactivities, making them well-suited as covalent reactivity handles.

title: Active, Scalable and Broadly Soluble Chain Transfer Precatalysts
abstract: Historically, cobalt(II) complexes have been shown to be highly potent catalytic chain transfer agents (CCTAs) in the linear or crosslinking polymerization of methacrylates. These transition metal species reversibly abstract hydrogen atoms (H˙) from propagating chains (P n ˙), terminating them as alkenes (P n =), and add them to monomers (M) to form new chains; this process is mechanistically categorized as a metal-hydride hydrogen atom transfer (MHAT).

title: Analytical approach to population, polarization and coherence dynamics of chirality induced spin selectivity model
abstract: We develop an analytical theory of chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) for two-electron radical-pair systems, treating spin-state preparation, coherent evolution, and spin-selective recombination within a unified framework. Starting from a Hamiltonian containing isotropic exchange, Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya (DM) interaction, and average and differential local fields, we derive exact two–level dynamics for singlet-triplet populations, spin polarization, and coherence, and compare chirality-induced spin polarization (CISP) with chirality-induced spin coherence (CISC).

title: Electrostatic Virus Capture and Post-Capture Containment Using Positively Charged Porous Polymer (P3) Beads for Point-of-use Water Treatment
abstract: Waterborne viruses remain an important challenge to drinking-water safety, particularly for point-of-use treatment where simple and effective technologies are needed. In this study, we develop positively charged porous polymer (P3) beads that couple electrostatic attraction with swelling-assisted transport for rapid virus capture and post-capture containment. The interconnected porous network provides extensive accessible internal charged surfaces while retaining a large bead size for simple physical separation after treatment.

title: Deoxofluorination of Formyl-Substituted Boronates: A Practical Entry to Difluoromethyl-Containing Organoboron Building Blocks
